Adopted `training/scripts/signal_hold_backtest.py` as the standard Rung-0 gate and added a caveat to `edge_probe.py` so its "NO_EDGE" reads as a worst-case bound, not a verdict. This creates no edge (the current signal still fails hold-aware) but ensures the NEXT candidate basis is judged correctly rather than falsely rejected — the actual root-cause fix available in code today.
- **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE (and why): no live architectural refactor / agent removal** (the working SMA200-hold rule is already live and certified; the evidence-only agent layer is by-design P228/P293d; removal is risk-without-benefit P377); **no DRL retrain** (every basis fails Rung-0); **no fee/gate weakening** (the P164/P179 fake-positive artifact). The "change other agents/strategies correspondingly" is written as the §4 SPEC, to be executed when a lever fires — not churned now on a clean, working live system.
- **Mitigation pattern:** when asked to "root-cause fix and change everything correspondingly" on a system whose problem is data/scale not code, the honest deliverable is (a) name the non-code root cause with evidence, (b) fix the one real code defect if there is one (here: the mis-measuring gate), and (c) specify the end-to-end changes as a GATED spec rather than executing a speculative refactor — a big correspondence-refactor on a working system is the risk-without-benefit trap (P377), and the plan's value is readiness, not motion.
### P386. [MEASURED 2026-08-24, operator: "at 4h tick we should HOLD if we predict up, not round-trip; derivatives produce revenue"] The operator was RIGHT — holding cuts cost ~20x and per-bar framing was wrong — but the ML signal still does not robustly beat hold; the smooth SMA200 rule does, and is already live [P386]
- **THE INSIGHT, and it corrects P385's framing.** The edge probe charged cost PER BAR as if every 4h prediction is a round trip — the worst-case execution. A weak-but-persistent signal should drive a HELD position: go long and STAY long while the sign persists, paying the fee only on FLIPS. `training/scripts/signal_hold_backtest.py` tests it properly — walk-forward ridge (same features as P385) -> deadband position (long z>+b, short z<-b, else HOLD previous) on a long/short PERP with funding carry, honest CDE cost on position CHANGES only, deadband swept.
- **HOLDING CUTS THE FEE BARRIER ~20x — the operator's core point, confirmed.** BTC cost by deadband: band 0 (react every bar) **287%**, band 1.0 **49%**, band 2.0 **14%**. The per-bar edge-probe framing was too pessimistic about execution; the fee is not a fixed wall, it scales with turnover, and holding collapses it.
- **BUT even held optimally the ML signal does NOT robustly beat buy-and-hold.** OOS 2023-11 -> 2026-07 (5,823 bars): BTC hold +82%/Sh0.44 vs best held-signal **band 1.0 +104%/Sh0.56** — real, but its neighbors are −50%/+2%/−27%, i.e. ONE lucky deadband, not pre-committable (the P243/P340 overfit-a-parameter signature; you cannot pick band=1.0 in advance without lookahead). ETH best band 2.0 +24% stays BELOW hold (+47%). SOL is NEGATIVE at every band (−153% to −324%) — anti-predictive when held. Funding carry negligible (+0 to −2%), so derivatives-funding is not a hidden revenue driver at this size; shorting is included and is what makes band-0 ruinous.
- **THE CONSTRUCTIVE RESULT: the insight is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED and it is the one thing that works.** A hold-while-signal-persists position on a SMOOTH, principled signal is exactly the live regimebook SMA200 rule (trades ~6-13x/yr), certified net-positive after cost on ETH/SOL (P321). So the system already does "hold when we predict up." What P386 shows is that the ML/DRL signal is NOT a better hold-signal than SMA200 — it is noisier, so its held version needs a lookahead-picked deadband, while the moving-average rule holds stably and is committable.
- **REFINED ANSWER: the barrier is not only the fee — holding removes most of it — the remaining barrier is SIGNAL QUALITY.** The IC~0.04 ML signal is too noisy to hold profitably in a way you could commit to; the SMA200 rule is not, and it is already the live decider. This does NOT re-open the DRL: the DRL churns (483 trades even at di=8, P381b) precisely because it does not hold like a smooth rule, and its held-equivalent is what P386 shows is overfit/below-hold. Backtest on the multiply-read window (P260 discount); a robust pass would have been a forward-shadow candidate, and there is none.
- **Mitigation pattern:** when a signal is weak, test it as a HELD position (fee on flips only) before concluding "fee-blocked" — per-bar cost is the worst case and overstates the barrier ~20x. But holding only rescues a signal SMOOTH enough to commit to a fixed rule; a noisy signal's held version wins at one swept parameter and fails at its neighbors, which is not a strategy. The live SMA200 rule is the smooth-signal instance that works; the ML signal is the noisy one that does not.
### P385. [MEASURED 2026-08-24, operator: "can we get the edge in this data at this scale after honest cost"] The signal IS real (IC ~0.04, t~3, all 3 assets) but ~2x too weak for the flat-fee floor — the binding constraint is the FEE/SCALE, quantified [P385]

Low turnover is how an edge survives a flat fee floor; a per-bar model cannot, because each trade is a fresh fee.

The mechanical path to contribute, unchanged (P200 ladder): a new basis must clear Rung-0 (cheap edge probe) -> retrain -> 30d forward shadow -> P166 gate -> only then the sleeve consumes it; DRL going ACTIVE is earned forward, never assumed. Genuinely-untested bases that COULD carry signal are acquisition projects (options-native term structure/OI/gamma, on-chain flows, cross-venue breadth), each gated on this same Rung-0 probe first. The honest lever remains fee/scale (P385): at 10bps RT the IC-0.04 signal already clears for ETH/SOL, so more capital / a percentage venue unlocks the CURRENT data without any new data at all.
- **[P385c — "do the two things + retrain GMM first?"] Cross-asset/breadth probed (5th new basis), NO PULSE; the GMM answer is consistency-not-edge; the fee lever is operator-only.** THING 1 (new data): probed cross-asset/breadth — breadth (fraction of 8 assets above SMA), cross-sectional dispersion, relative strength, BTC-dominance momentum, cross-asset lead-lag — the one readily-available basis the single-asset DRL lacks, over 6y of all 8 assets (`training/scripts/breadth_edge_probe.py`, report `breadth_edge_probe_p385.json`). That makes FIVE independent bases (single-asset P385, higher-freq flow P375b, L2 depth P379, tick microstructure P385b, cross-asset breadth here) all at the SAME ceiling: extractable IC ~0.04-0.05, ~half the flat-fee floor. The ceiling is the information content of 4H crypto direction at this scale, not any model/feature gap. THING 2 (drop the fee floor): operator-only (percentage venue / more capital), not codeable; already quantified (P385: 10bps unlocks ETH/SOL — and SOL breadth's 0.045 would clear there too). GMM-BEFORE-DRL: YES when the data basis changes, because the GMM GENERATES the DRL's regime features and must be refit split-aware on the exact training data (P215/P164 — else leakage/skew), refit as part of the parquet rebuild, paired atomically. But it is a CONSISTENCY requirement, NOT an edge lever — P385 measured the regime feature group at IC ~0.01-0.015, so a fresh GMM cannot move the 0/21 verdict. On the current data no refit is needed (p381 verified `[CLEAN-GMM] split_aware`). NET: I did the executable thing (probe new data first, P200 ladder) and correctly did NOT retrain DRL — every probed basis fails Rung-0, so a retrain (with or without a GMM refit) reproduces the negative. Retrain only when a basis clears the gate; the readily-available ones do not, and the honest unlock is fee/scale.
- **Mitigation pattern:** "is there edge after cost?" is two questions — is the signal REAL (here yes, IC 0.04 t~3), and does it clear the FEE (here no, at this scale). Answer them separately and quantify the fee at which the answer flips; "no edge" without that decomposition hides that the constraint is the venue/scale, not the data.

The live gate prices the REAL CDE fee, which is FLAT ~$0.60/contract (`core/cde_fees.py`, P315), i.e. **9.4-14.5bps per leg for maker AND taker alike** at nano notional. Measured maker-first saving: **BTC 0.98 / ETH 1.46 / SOL 0.00 bps per round trip** — nothing. Break-even maker fill fraction: BTC f≈0.30 (ETH/SOL clear at f=0), and BTC fails it four ways over — observed f≈0 (the CDE fill ledger `data/fill_quality.jsonl` holds 173 rows, ALL pre-P290 Kraken-era, ZERO CDE-format), adverse selection erases the ~3bps margin (a trend entry posts WITH the move → ~30% fill rate and the fills you get are the ones that ran through you, arXiv:2502.18625), the gate rejects BTC by ~12bps regardless, and BTC's forward edge is itself ~0 (funding-leg increment FAIL, CI spans zero). The live gate is structurally MORE conservative than reality (charges taker fee + FULL spread on both legs + a 0.75 haircut), and it is NOT rejecting realizable-profitable trades: ETH/SOL clear taker cost by 2-6x, BTC genuinely should not trade.
- **COST DECOMPOSITION (the decisive measurement, RT bps):** BTC fixed-fee 19.74 + spread 1.58 + impact 6.38 = 27.7 vs edge 24.1 -> **net -3.6**; ETH 29.02+5.26+9.72=44.0 vs 88.1 -> **+44.1**; SOL 29.02+2.65+9.33=41.0 vs 221.7 -> **+180.7**. The FIXED per-contract fee is the dominant term and only amortizes with NOTIONAL — maker touches ~1bps of it. Because the fee is flat-$/contract, **BTC's cost in bps FALLS as price rises with zero added capital**: at $100k BTC net +10.5, at $140k +14, at $200k +16.5.

- **STREAM 3 (external best-practice, net-of-cost only) — corroborates every internal finding and names the honest playbook.** No published crypto-trend result is net-profitable at edge-approx-cost + fixed-cost floor + 3 assets + ~$11k; every net-profitable result runs at edge >> cost via breadth (150 assets), intermediate horizon (H6), and PERCENTAGE fees with no fixed floor (Nguyen 2026, arXiv:2602.11708). The net-return levers that exist: (1) STOP trading BTC (edge < cost — Garleanu-Pedersen; **already implemented**, P321 stops BTC at the gate); (2) edge-to-cost entry gating (**already implemented** — the gate does exactly this); (3) horizon extension has a floor and the book is already slow. - **Mitigation patterns:** (a) "solve completely" for a profitability problem decomposes into signal / execution / capital — run each to exhaustion and name which one binds, rather than searching the exhausted one harder (P269/P283); (b) a fee quoted as a percentage (0/3bps) is a MODEL, and when the venue charges a flat per-contract fee the maker/taker distinction is nearly worthless at small notional — decompose fixed-vs-variable before pricing any execution lever; (c) a research verdict from a subagent is a claim to verify (P290) — all three streams' load-bearing numbers were reconciled against the live fee model at the call site before being recorded.

Both are invisible to `grep` and to a code reader; only `repr()` of the file showed them. **Use the Write/Edit tools for any content containing escapes** — I concluded this earlier in the same session and reached for the heredoc again three times.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) when you hit a trap yourself, AUDIT before assuming the codebase shares it — here the answer was "8 of 9 already correct", and the honest output was a guard rather than a fix; (b) a check hand-rolled twice in two days is a missing roster, and the roster must be derived from what it covers or it is a list someone has to remember to update; (c) `repr()` the file when a regex "obviously correct" in isolation fails against it — a mangled escape is invisible in every other view.

### P362. [FIXED 2026-08-21, operator: "fix all remaining tasks"] A refusal that asserted one cause, and the cause had rotted — it misled me while I was sweeping for outstanding work
Continuing the P361 sweep through the standing instruments. The evidence pipeline is healthy — **10 Monday cron jobs installed and running**, reports at 2026-08-10 and 08-17, the P237 tripwire reading `armed 2/2 closed` on all three assets with 08-24 and 08-31 still to come, so it lands exactly on its 2026-09-01 date gate. What was broken was the message I got when I ran the tripwire from the wrong place. Tests `tests/test_p362_tripwire_refusal_cause.py` (5); four falsification probes red-then-restored.
- **THE DEFECT: `tripwire_check` printed one cause for two different states, and the cause it named had gone stale.** Whenever it found no reports it said *"no slope_*.json under &lt;dir&gt; — the weekly calibrator has not written there yet (first cron run 2026-08-11)"*. True when written. **False since 2026-08-10**, because the calibrator has written every Monday since. Run from a laptop it told me the calibrator had not run **while the server held two reports in that exact directory**, and the real cause — this tool reads the CONTAINER's data volume (P213) — was never mentioned.
- **An alert must name its cause from the DATA, not from a guess baked into the format string** (P155, where a veto told the operator to "check VETO_CHAIN logs" while the veto chain was innocent and silent). And **a hardcoded date inside a refusal is a claim that rots invisibly**, because the refusal path is the one nobody reads until something is already wrong.
- **Split into the two states, which is the same missing-vs-neutral distinction this file keeps making (P2/P199): *I could not look* vs *I looked and found nothing*.** A missing directory now names the wrong environment and prints the exact `docker exec` command, and explicitly says it is **not** a statement about the cron; an existing-but-empty directory still blames the cron, because when the directory really is there that IS the thing to check. Quieting the wrong cause must not quiet the right one (P248). Both branches keep P199's "this is not a verdict" clause and exit 2, pinned.
- **Two smaller things worth keeping from the same minute.** `echo "exit=$?"` after a pipeline reports **`tail`'s** status, not the script's — it printed `exit=0` for a tool that had correctly returned 2 (the P185 trap, live). And the test suite for this drives the tool through **`run_cli`**, the P360 harness, which makes it the second adoption of that helper and the first outside its own test file.
- **A probe of mine was INVALID on an anchor**: I wrote the `old` text as the f-string source including its quotes, and the file's line wraps differently. Fixed by anchoring on the message text itself. Cheap, and the harness caught it before it could report a false pass.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) any refusal that names a cause should be checked against the case where that cause is FALSE — refusal paths are exercised rarely and rot silently, so the message is usually written once and never re-read until it misleads someone; (b) "I could not look" and "I looked and found nothing" need different messages and often different fixes, and a tool that collapses them costs a diagnosis every time it fires; (c) `cmd | tail` then `$?` reads the LAST stage's status — check exit codes without a pipeline, or a refusal reads as a pass.

### P360. [BUILT 2026-08-21, operator quoted my own paragraph back] The INVOCATION chooses the assertion — 24 test files drive a CLI through a subprocess, which caps every one of them at presence-only
I closed P359 by noting in passing that adopting it "forced a real change: P358b's test drove the CLI in a subprocess, where the table cannot be neutralised at all — so the strongest available check was structurally out of reach and I hadn't noticed." The operator quoted that back. It is a bigger finding than the aside I filed it as. Helper `tests/_cli_harness.py`; tests `tests/test_p360_cli_harness.py` (13); six falsification probes red-then-restored.
- **THE CLASS, and it is about what a test can even ASK rather than about a bug.** `subprocess.run([sys.executable, ...])` is the obvious way to test a CLI, and **a subprocess cannot be patched, neutralised or inspected from the parent.** So such a test is structurally incapable of asking anything stronger than *"the output contains X"* — it can never establish that X came from anywhere in particular. P358b's was written that way, and when P359 built `assert_drives_output` the strongest available check simply could not be applied. **Choosing the invocation had silently chosen the weakest assertion.**
- **Measured: 24 test files drive a repo script with `sys.executable`.** Every one carries the same cap. That is a population, not an incident.
- **AND SUBPROCESS WAS THE RIGHT INSTINCT, which is exactly why the trap works.** This repo's tools carry deliberately distinct exit codes — `ci_status` 0/1/2/3/4, `compute_shadow_ic` 2 vs 3, `seat_check` 2 vs 3 — and P185 records testing "both refusal paths at real exit-code level". Calling `main()` directly loses the code unless you handle `SystemExit`, so subprocess is the *safe* way to get it, and taking the weak assertion along with it is invisible. **The fix is therefore not "stop using subprocess" — it is that the cheap path must not also be the weak one.**
- **`run_cli` returns the exit code AND leaves the module patchable**, resolving the code the way a shell does (`SystemExit` wins, else the return value, else 0; `None` is 0). Without that it would be a downgrade and nobody would take it — pinned by three tests, because the moment the exit code is lossy the helper stops being adopted and the class comes straight back.
- **WHEN SUBPROCESS IS STILL RIGHT is written into the module header rather than left to judgement**, because a helper that reads as "always use me" gets used where it is wrong: process-level behaviour (an import-time `SystemExit`, a crash, `-X utf8` encoding — P294), a script that must run against a DIFFERENT tree (a worktree, P328/P344 — importing the parent's copy measures the wrong subject), and cases where global-state isolation is load-bearing, since in-process execution shares `sys.modules`, logging handlers and `os.environ` with the session.
- **Fail directions pinned:** `sys.argv` is restored in a `finally`, so a crashing CLI cannot leak a rewritten argv into every later test (P186); `load_cli` must NOT run `main()`, or merely inspecting a CLI would execute it; stdout and stderr stay separate; a missing entry point is a loud refusal.
- **A probe found `CliResult.module` was DECORATION — a field nothing read, in the helper built one hour after the detector for exactly that (P170/P359).** Its first mutation was VACUOUS too, and there the PROBE was the defect: adding a default to the last NamedTuple field changes nothing while `run_cli` still passes `mod` explicitly, so the mutation had to be at the CONSTRUCTION site. The field now earns its place with a test showing the PATH caller gets a handle back and can neutralise the table without a second `load_cli` — which is the whole difference from subprocess.
- **Adopted at the site that produced the finding** (P345: a second uncalled helper would be the joke writing itself) — P358b's hand-rolled `importlib` + `redirect_stdout` is replaced by `load_cli`, and a test asserts the harness has a caller outside its own file. **Honest scope: 1 of 24 converted.** The other 23 are working tests, and rewiring them for tidiness is the risk P141 exists to prevent; what this buys is that the next author has somewhere to look, and that the cap is now written down instead of rediscovered.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) before writing a test, ask what its INVOCATION makes impossible — subprocess forbids patching, a source scan forbids behaviour, a mock forbids integration, and each choice caps the strongest question you can ask without ever announcing it; (b) when the safe way to get one property (an exit code) costs another (patchability), build the thing that gives both, or every author will keep paying the same silent price; (c) an aside in a summary that begins "and I hadn't noticed" is a finding wearing a footnote's clothes — this one turned out to describe 24 files.

### P359. [BUILT 2026-08-21, operator quoted my own paragraph back] "I checked the table and not its use" — the fourth hand-rolled fix for one class, given a mechanism
I closed P358b by reporting that a probe setting `_cause = None` left every test green, that this was the third vacuous guard of the day, and that I had replaced it with a behavioural test. The operator quoted that back. **A lesson recorded in prose is the thing this file exists to convert into a mechanism (P280/P328)** — the same move that produced P344, P350 and P357. Helper `tests/_guard_pins.assert_drives_output`; tests `tests/test_p359_drives_output.py` (7); four falsification probes red-then-restored.
- **THE CLASS, and it is older than today: P170 named it in April** ("a mechanism nothing calls is decoration") and every fix since has been rewritten from scratch, a different way each time:
  | | |
  |---|---|
  | P312 | a producer's report-building seam that nothing called |
  | P324 | `main()` no longer calling `decide_verdict` |
  | P357 | a `done()` check the test could not reach at all |
  | P358b | `KNOWN_SILENT_CAUSES` verified for shape while `_cause = None` collapsed every label and left ALL tests green |
  Four hand-rolled pins for one class is the signature of a **missing affordance rather than of carelessness** — the identical reading that produced `Probe.near` in P357 after four rounds of sibling ambiguity.
- **THE INSIGHT THE HELPER ENCODES: presence cannot distinguish CONSUMED from COINCIDENTAL.** A test that looks for a value in the output passes whether the consumer read the table or produced that value some other way — which is exactly what happened in P358b, where the label came from a literal fallback. **Only VARYING the input and watching the output change settles it.** So `assert_drives_output(run, marker, disable)` runs the real consumer TWICE — once as-is, once with the data neutralised — and requires the marker to appear and then DISAPPEAR. That is a falsification probe executed inline on every run, rather than one a human has to think to run.
  - Its own decisive probe makes the point: a consumer that FABRICATES the right-looking label without reading the table (`_cause = ('STRUCTURAL', 'x P358 P141')`) passes every presence check and is caught here.
- **Both vacuity directions are refused, because the helper is itself a guard.** A marker absent even WITH the data in place fails loudly (the test would otherwise pass for a consumer that never produced it — P174 in the direction nobody checks), and restoration sits in a `finally` so an exploding consumer cannot leave the table neutralised for everything after it (P186: a test mutating shared state). A `disable` that restores itself — a monkeypatch fixture — may return `None`.
- **ADOPTED, not shipped beside its own test.** P345's lesson (a second uncalled helper would have been the joke writing itself): P358b's test is re-expressed through it, which required making the consumer in-process — the old version drove the CLI in a **subprocess**, where the table cannot be neutralised at all, so the strongest available check was structurally out of reach. A test asserts the helper has a caller outside its own file, so it cannot decay into the decoration it detects.
- **Honest scope:** one adopted site today; P312's and P324's pins are named as the adoption surface and are NOT converted — both would need their `main()` driven end to end, which is a rewrite of two working tests rather than a mechanism, and P345's rule is that rewiring working sites for tidiness is the risk P141 exists to prevent.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) when a fix for one class has been hand-rolled four times, stop writing the fifth and ask what affordance is missing — the fourth instance is the evidence, not the coincidence; (b) any test that asserts a value APPEARS should ask what it would do if the consumer produced that value some other way, and if the answer is "pass", it is measuring presence and not causation; (c) the cheapest way to prove causation in a test is the same as in a probe — remove the input and require the output to change.

### P358. [MEASURED 2026-08-21, operator quoted my own closing paragraph back] The silent DECIDE agent costs 0.1%, its silence is not the market being quiet, and both halves of my "retire it or repair it" were wrong
I closed P357 with *"kraken_quant holds DECIDE authority and contributes nothing … retiring the authority or repairing its reachable surface is a live-behaviour change, so it stays recorded."* Measuring it corrected me twice, and the correction is the entry. Tests `tests/test_p358_kraken_quant_silence.py` (10); five falsification probes red-then-restored. **Nothing armed** — every remedy below is a P141 decision.

**1. "RETIRE THE AUTHORITY" TARGETS A COST OF UNDER 0.1%, so it was the wrong lever.** The live pool is exactly `['quant','kraken_quant']`, so fusion takes its MULTI-decider branch every tick. LAYER 3's abstention rule (FIX-1/P71) drops abstainers from the AGREEMENT ratio — **but the weighting loop below it iterates every DECIDE agent and adds `max(conf,0.01)**2` to `total_weight` regardless**, so a silent agent contributes `1e-4`:
  `final_direction = D·C²/(C²+1e-4)` and `avg_conf = √(C²+1e-4)`.
  Measured over every retained `[AGENT-TRACE]`, quant's confidence takes exactly three values and none is near the floor: **0.90 (131 obs), 0.33 (87), 1.00 (21)**. At 0.90/1.00 the SOLO-conviction branch fires and passes `best_conf` through **exactly** untouched; at 0.33 the `else` branch inflates confidence by **+0.046%**. Direction is diluted by **at most 0.09% — and the sleeve sizes by the SIGN (P293d), so that is a literal no-op on live orders.** Removing the authority would be churn on a live account for a measured tenth of a percent of a magnitude nothing reads. **I anchored a recommendation to the loud fact (a DECIDE agent is silent) instead of the priced one.**
  - The counter-case is pinned rather than left implicit: at `C=0.01` the abstainer takes **half** the weight. The bound above is a property of quant's OBSERVED confidence, not of the formula, and if any decider ever publishes near the floor this disposition does not carry.

**2. "ONLY 2 OF 12 REACHABLE" WAS STALE — it is 6, and P217 is why.** I quoted P215's number without checking whether a later entry had moved it. **P217 added `STEADY_UPTREND` and `NEUTRAL_DRIFT` to `_REGIME_MAP`**, and with `MOMENTUM_RALLY` live the BULL bucket is active too. A check that cannot fire (P174), in a DECIDE-authority agent.
  - **`DarkPoolVolume` reads a shape the converter never builds.** It asks for `market_data[asset]['volume'/'close']`, while `_convert_market_data` returns a FIXED key set (`prices`, `bid_depth`, `ask_depth`, …) with **no per-asset sub-dict** — so both reads are 0 and it `continue`s past all three assets. The P2 reader/writer mismatch. Worth stating precisely because I first suspected the converter was missing entirely and it is not: `prices`/`bid_depth`/`ask_depth` **are** built correctly, which is what makes the one absent shape easy to miss.
  - `RelativeStrength` and `KalmanCointegration` need **≥50 samples in an in-memory buffer** fed ~3 times per 4H tick — days of uninterrupted uptime, no persistence, reset on every deploy. The P301/P316 warmup class, for which `strategies/_warmup_state.py` is the built precedent.

**4. THE DISPOSITION, replacing the false binary.** The authority is not the problem and removing it buys ~0.1% of nothing. What is real is that **two reachable strategies are structurally incapable of firing and two more are starved by a clock the deploy cadence never allows** — so the DECIDE seat is vacuous for reasons that have nothing to do with market conditions. **Repairing any of them is an ARMING**: it would let a DECIDE-authority agent begin emitting directions on a live account, which is P141's boundary, not a bugfix to slip in behind a diagnosis.
  - So the pins are written the P318 way — they assert the defects are STILL THERE, and each failure message says that the strategy may now be live at DECIDE authority and needs an operator decision. A future author who "fixes" the depth split or adds a per-asset sub-dict gets told what they have just armed instead of discovering it from a trade.

**5. Sibling anchor ambiguity, fifth time in four entries — and this time the mechanism caught it before I did.** My probe anchored on `AUTHORITY_MATRIX_NORMAL`, which occurs twice (the definition and its use), and P357's `near` refusal named the count and the reason rather than editing the wrong matrix. That is the affordance working: the cost was one line, not a round trip through a red suite.

**6. [P358b] THE DIAGNOSTIC NOW SEPARATES THE THREE CAUSES — the one thing here that is not an operator decision.** It printed six identical `[DEAD] 0 fires` lines for three distinct states, so a reader could not tell a strategy that CANNOT fire from one that is starved from one that simply declined: the P199/P216 conflation, inside the tool built to explain the silence. `KNOWN_SILENT_CAUSES` labels the four measured ones **[STRUCTURAL]** / **[WARMUP]** with the arithmetic and, for the structural pair, the sentence that repairing them is a **P141 arming**. The residue keeps `cause UNKNOWN, worth a trace` — naming what is known is only useful if it leaves the unexplained set visible (2 of 6: `FundingDivergenceStrategy`, `ETFSpotCointegration`).
- **My first cut covered 2 of 4 and said nothing, and only running it against REAL producer output showed it.** I keyed the table on CLASS names (`OrderBookImbalanceStrategy`) while the agent reports the `name` each strategy passes to `BaseStrategy.__init__` (`OrderBookImbalance`, `KalmanCointegration_SOL_ETH`) — so two entries matched nothing and the tool printed `cause UNKNOWN` for defects it had just been told about. **P310/P2 inside a fix for a conflation**, and P264/P309's rule again: a consumer's first run against real producer output is part of shipping it. The guard now reads the roster from the PRODUCER (instantiating the classes and reading `.name`), because a hardcoded mirror here is the drift it exists to catch.
- **And a probe caught the guard being decoration.** Setting `_cause = None` collapsed every label back to `[DEAD] 0 fires` and **every test stayed green** — I had checked the TABLE and not its USE (P170). **Third vacuous guard of mine caught this way today.** Replaced with a behavioural test that drives the real CLI over a synthetic stats file and asserts `[STRUCTURAL]`, `[WARMUP]` and `P141` reach the output.
- **Mitigation pattern (d):** when a label is added to explain a state, the test must assert the label REACHES THE OUTPUT, not merely that the lookup table is well-formed — a correct table nothing consults renders exactly like no table at all.

**7. [P358c] THE TWO `cause UNKNOWN` STRATEGIES TRACED — the residue is empty, and the picture is worse than P358 said.** P358b deliberately left them visible as the set worth investigating; this is that investigation.
  | strategy | cause | detail |
  |---|---|---|
  | OrderBookImbalance | **STRUCTURAL** | `bid ≡ ask ≡ depth/2` → imbalance identically 0 |
  | DarkPoolVolume | **STRUCTURAL** | reads `market_data[asset]['volume'/'close']`; no per-asset sub-dict |
  | **ETFSpotCointegration** | **STRUCTURAL** | reads `close`/`open`/`volume_24h`; the converter produces **none** of them, so `btc_close == 0` and it returns on its first check |
  | RelativeStrength | WARMUP | ≥50 price samples ≈ 17 ticks ≈ **2.8 days** uptime |
  | KalmanCointegration_SOL_ETH | WARMUP | ≥50 price AND ≥30 spread (spread only accrues once prices are full) ≈ 27 ticks ≈ **4.5 days** |
  | FundingDivergence | WARMUP | **≥240** price samples ≈ 80 ticks ≈ **13.3 days** — the longest clock of the six |
- **So it is 3 of 6 structurally dead, not 2** — ETFSpotCointegration is the same P2 shape as DarkPoolVolume, and I had it filed as unexplained. **And the surviving three are bounded by 2.8–13.3 days of UNINTERRUPTED uptime with no persistence** (P301/P316's class), on an engine P341 measured at ~10 deploys in a single day. **The DECIDE seat is therefore not merely quiet — half its reachable surface cannot fire at all and the other half is gated on a clock the deploy cadence never allows.** That is a sharper statement of P358's finding and it strengthens the disposition: the authority is still not the thing to remove, and repairing any of the six is still a P141 arming.
- **The day figures are arithmetic over thresholds, so the THRESHOLDS are pinned, not the prose** — `samples / 3 appends per tick × 4h`; if a threshold moves the figure is silently wrong, which is how a measured claim rots into a quoted one (the P228 shape this entry already committed once).
- **The residue guard was re-expressed rather than deleted.** It asserted a real strategy still read as `cause UNKNOWN`; with all six traced that is no longer true, so it now uses a SYNTHETIC name — the property being protected is that naming the known causes never hides the set worth tracing, not that the set is non-empty today.

- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) before recommending that a component be removed, PRICE what it currently costs — "it contributes nothing" and "it costs something" are different claims, and here the second was ~0.1% of a quantity the execution layer discards; (b) when an agent is silent, separate *cannot fire* from *chose not to* before proposing either a removal or a repair — the diagnostic reported six identical `[DEAD] 0 fires` lines for three distinct causes, which is the P199/P216 conflation one level down; (c) a number quoted from an older entry is a claim with a date on it: P215's "2 of 12" was true when written and had been superseded by P217 for two weeks.

### P357. [AUDITED + BUILT 2026-08-21, operator: "check we have sufficient agent/model to support trading in kraken and coinbase" + quoted two of my own limitations back] The venue-sufficiency answer is ONE decider and ZERO trained models — and the two limitations I had recorded as prose each got a mechanism
Two requests in one message. The audit is measurement only (nothing was armed — every remedy it points at is a P141 decision); the two mechanisms are `main.py::_spawn_bg` and `tools/falsify.Probe.near`. Tests `tests/test_p357_bg_task_death_and_probe_near.py` (17) + the P356 suite corrected (13 → 14); **eleven falsification probes red-then-restored**; full suite 6,122 green; gate clean, zero baseline movement, mypy unchanged at the standing 1084.

**PART 1 — IS THE AGENT/MODEL LAYER SUFFICIENT? Measured, and the honest answer is narrower than the roster suggests.**
- **KRAKEN CANNOT TRADE, BY CONFIGURATION, AND NO AGENT CHANGES THAT.** `data/coinbase_routing_state.json` reads `{"phase":"DUAL_VENUE","coinbase_assets":["BTC","ETH","SOL"],"kraken_assets":[]}`. With all three routed, P152 skips every new Kraken entry and the book has been empty since 2026-06-12, so "sufficient agents for Kraken" is not a question about agents — it is the recorded P152/P275 design. Asking it of the sleeve is the only version that has an answer.
- **THE CENSUS, over 348 asset-ticks of `[AGENT-TRACE]` in the retained logs — 19 agents seen, 10 ever directional, 9 never:**
  | agent | directional / seen | note |
  |---|---|---|
  | drl | 348 / 348 | **SHADOW — consumed by nothing** (P198) |
  | quant | 230 / 348 | the DECIDER (regimebook seat) |
  | sentiment | 177 / 348 | ADVISE, zero-weighted (P228) |
  | llm_sentiment | 174 / 348 | ADVISE, weighted |
  | options | 151 / 348 | ADVISE, weighted |
  | flow | 144 / 348 | ADVISE, weighted |
  | model_alpha | 135 / 348 | ADVISE, zero-weighted |
  | whale | 57 / 348 | ADVISE, weighted |
  | funding | 36 / 348 | ADVISE, weighted |
  | micro | 4 / 348 | P316 warmup |
  | **kraken_quant** | **0 / 348** | **DECIDE authority, silent** |
- **THE DECISIVE ARITHMETIC: only DECIDE agents ever set `result.direction`** (P293d — every other layer moves `base_exposure`, which the sleeve discards by sizing on the SIGN). There are two DECIDE agents; one of them emitted nothing in 348 asset-ticks. **So the system has exactly ONE decider — a rule book — and the 22 remaining agents cannot change a direction no matter what they say.** `DRLRuntime={gate=SHADOW|infer=SHADOW|promo=SHADOW|exec=OFF}` and `Quant=REAL(regimebook)`: **zero trained models are on the live decision path**, which is not a defect but the accumulated verdict of P198 (TQC demoted on live IC), P200/P241/P258 (0/39 folds promotable), P281 (every trained class dead at honest cost) and P285c (the one certified candidate withdrawn by its own seed probe).
- **THEREFORE "sufficient" splits in two, and the two halves have opposite answers.** *Mechanically* sufficient: the decider produces a direction, the gate prices it, the sleeve executes it, and the P356 disarm removed the last non-design blocker. *Evidentially* thin: one certified rule book carries everything, and its measured per-round-trip edge (P321's era-median 24.1/88.1/221.7bps) is what the whole account rests on. **The scarce resource is not agents, it is DECIDERS with evidence** — and this file records that adding agents has never been the constraint (P228: 12 ADVISE agents are deliberately zero-weighted because no forward evidence clears the bar; P293d: an ADVISE weight is a measured no-op on live orders).
- **`kraken_quant` at 0/348 is the one finding worth acting on**, and it is not new — P215 measured that only **2 of its 12 strategies are reachable** in the regime that has prevailed, and both are archived-adjacent. It holds DECIDE authority and contributes nothing; that is a P141 decision (retire the authority, or fix the reachable surface), not a fix to make silently.

**PART 2 — "ITS SILENCE PROVES NOTHING EITHER WAY", given a mechanism.**
- **P356 fixed the discarded-Task reference and had to report the fix as LATENT, because it could not tell a live background loop from a dead one.** The reason was in the entry: `OnChainFeed.start()` logs only on a *caught* fetch error, so an empty log is what a healthy feed and a collected one both produce.
- **THE HALF NOBODY HAD NAMED IS WORSE THAN THE WEAK REFERENCE, and it is a property of asyncio rather than of this repo: a Task that raises STORES the exception and reports it to nobody.** Nothing surfaces unless somebody calls `.exception()`. So the failure mode written in the comment directly above the defect — *"OnChainFeed ... stay dormant → dead signals for months"* — was not merely unnoticed, it was **unnoticeable**: no traceback, no log line, no exit code. Holding a reference stops a task being collected and does nothing whatever about a task dying.
- **`_spawn_bg` closes both halves in one place** (the six dispatch sites each had to remember, which is how one of them would eventually not). The done-callback retrieves the exception and reports at the severity that matches what happened: **ERROR with the traceback** for a raise, naming the task and the CONSEQUENCE (*"the signals it feeds are now stale and nothing else will say so"* — P240, an alert must say what it means); **WARNING** for a clean return, because a supposedly-endless loop returning is a different fault and collapsing it into the healthy case would make it invisible the way the raise was; **INFO** for a shutdown cancellation, because a report that alarms on every shutdown becomes wallpaper (P202).
- **`background_task_names()` is the POSITIVE half and it is the one that answers the original question.** A death report answers *"did it stop?"*; the 4H heartbeat's new `bg:` segment answers *"is it running right now?"*, which had no answer at all. An empty list renders as **`bg: NONE RUNNING`**, never as an empty field that reads like a healthy one. **After this, silence is evidence.**
- **Fail directions pinned:** retrieving the exception is itself wrapped, because the callback runs inside the event loop and a raise there would convert an observability fix into an outage (the P85 shape, in the guard); and a task that has finished is never reported alive.

**PART 3 — SIBLING ANCHOR AMBIGUITY, FOUR TIMES IN THREE ENTRIES, given a mechanism.**
- P355's pin matched the terminal handler as well as the transient one it meant; two P356 probes matched both `BinanceTakerMonitor` and `LeadLagAlphaEngine`, whose `__init__` signatures are identical. **The harness caught all four — the refusal is correct and stays.** What was missing was any way to PROCEED: the author's only remedy was to hand-expand the anchor into a multi-line block until it happened to be unique, which is fragile in the opposite direction (a wider anchor breaks on any edit to the lines it swept up).
- **`assert_text_pin` already solved this for PINS in P350 with `near=`.** The probe harness did not have it — so the concept was absent from the tool where the mistake kept happening, which is P171/P226 applied to a helper rather than to a fix. `Probe.near` scopes the search to a window around a unique anchor, and **`near` must itself be unique**, or an ambiguous anchor scopes the probe to a window the author never read (P238 one level up).
- **ITS OWN DEMONSTRATION THEN FAILED TWICE, ON TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS OF MINE, AND BOTH ARE NOW PINNED.** (a) The first cut searched **FORWARD ONLY**, and in the real case the distinguishing text sits *after* the probed line — a helper whose name says "nearby" must not silently mean "after" (P350's lesson about a docstring overstating its guarantee; `assert_text_pin` is forward-only and *documents* it, which is the right trade for a pin whose anchor is chosen to precede). (b) The window was **4000 chars**, which for anything but a large file is no scoping at all — both siblings land inside it and the probe is refused for "2 within the window", the same dead end `near` exists to remove. **P350 made this exact correction to `assert_text_pin` (1500 → 400)**; the default is now 600 with `near_window=` to override, and the direction is deliberate: too small only ever REFUSES, too large silently stops discriminating.
- **A third defect, and this one was in a GUARD rather than in a fix.** A probe came back **VACUOUS**: reverting `list(assets)` in `LeadLagAlphaEngine` left every test green, because P356's copy-by-reference test covered `BinanceTakerMonitor` only — it fixed both siblings and pinned one. **P171/P226 for the third time in one entry**, and it was found by the harness reporting a gap in the *guard*, which is the whole reason to run probes rather than to read code. Parametrized over both classes; the probe then falsifies.
- **A fourth, in the probe I wrote for the sibling-ambiguity fix itself:** my chosen anchor `name="sol_onchain"` occurs twice (paper and live). Recorded at the site rather than quietly corrected, because it is the cleanest possible demonstration that the class is not an attention problem.
- **The vacuous-guard scoreboard for this entry: three of my own guards were too weak and every one printed as a passing line before the probe ran.** Including one — `if not t.done()` — that my test could not reach at all, since a completed task is discarded before the test looks; the replacement CONSTRUCTS the window `done()` protects (between completion and `call_soon` running the callback) instead of hoping to land in it.
**PART 4 — [P357b, same day] AND THE COMMIT WENT RED, ON THE SECOND SILENT-DROP CASE IN `isolate_commit`.**
- **P352b built that tool's refusal for hunks carrying NO marker, and REASONED the marked ones away** in its own docstring: *"a dropped hunk that carries somebody else's marker is attributable and passes quietly."* **That sentence is false in the common case.** A hunk that EDITS a line stamped by an earlier entry of your OWN campaign carries that earlier marker in its added text, and is indistinguishable — to a marker match — from another session's work.
- **Measured: five of six dispatch-site rewrites modified lines tagged `# [P356]`**, so `--marker "[P357]"` dropped them **silently**, the tool printed success, and the commit went out with **one sixth** of the change in it. Both CI workflows red. **The same silent partial commit P352b exists to end, one case over** — and invisible for the same reason, because every check below the drop still passes.
- **Attributed against WORKTREES of the commit and its parent, not the working tree** — the local gate was CLEAN while CI was red, because a parallel session's uncommitted work masked the delta (P311b: the working tree cannot tell you what you committed). Parent 711 findings and clean; my commit 712; the unique-pair diff names the single addition, `self.background_task_names()` inside the pre-existing heartbeat try (which must stay — P227). Hand-bumped that one counter with the attribution, never `--update` (P171). A `git archive` tree was tried first and **correctly refused** — P158 will not run git-grep-based scanners without a `.git`, which is exactly why P328 uses a worktree.
- **Fixed as a NOTE, not a refusal, and that is a decision:** in a shared tree most foreign hunks really are foreign, and refusing on every one would make the tool unusable for the situation it exists for — a guard that fires on the normal case gets bypassed (P202/P303). It now lists each foreign-marked drop **with its markers and its added lines**, so the author can recognise their own campaign's number. The remedy it names — stamp the line with BOTH markers — is pinned by a test, because advice that does not work is worse than silence.
- **A probe of mine came back VACUOUS here too, and the probe was the defect:** `endswith(marker)` still matches a line ending `# [P356] [P357]`. Replaced with a mutation that rejects any line carrying more than one marker, which is precisely the remedy under test. **Fourteen probes red-then-restored across the entry; four of my own guards and two of my own probes were too weak, and every one printed as a passing line first.**

**PART 5 — [P357c, one hour after the deploy] AND THE MECHANISM'S FIRST LIVE HEARTBEAT REPORTED TWO FEEDS DEAD THAT WERE FINE.**
- **Operator pasted two live FastRiskTick CRITICALs. Both turned out to be the system working exactly as designed** — and checking them is what surfaced the defect. `SOL: EXIT_ONLY - price_move=3.1%` was followed one second later by `[FastRiskTick][SLEEVE] SOL: EXIT_ONLY -> EXITED (execute_target(0) -> OK)` and, 37 seconds later, by the same trigger logged at INFO because the asset was now FLAT — the P240 downgrade confirming the flatten. The four `ETH: REDUCE_50 - depth_drop=72..83%` CRITICALs each landed on a `HTTPError: 500` from Coinbase and each produced `-> SKIPPED_STALE (venue snapshot stale — refusing to act)`: P141's refusal, with P329 keeping it out of the 30-minute backoff, and P240's `None`-keeps-full-severity rule correctly leaving them CRITICAL because the position was UNKNOWN rather than absent. **The depth reading was real, not a degraded feed** — Kraken showed ETH's 1% book at $1.48M two minutes later against a $4.77M anchor — which is the question P240 added the raw numerator and denominator to make answerable.
- **THE REAL FINDING WAS MINE, and it was in the entry above.** The first heartbeat read `bg: onchain_feed` and the boot log carried two WARNINGs: *"lead_lag ENDED without an error … whatever it feeds stops updating from now on"* and the same for `sol_onchain`. **Both are false.** P356 had already measured and written down that only `OnChainFeed.start()` runs its poll loop INLINE, while `LeadLagAlphaEngine.start()` and the SOL agent **spawn tracked inner tasks and return** — I quoted that sentence in the P357 test file and still wrote a blanket WARNING treating every clean return as a fault.
- **An alert that fires on the NORMAL case is how a real one becomes wallpaper (P202/P303)** — and here it is worse than noise, because it makes the one return that genuinely matters (the inline loop stopping) indistinguishable from the two that never mattered. The mechanism built so silence would be evidence spent its first hour generating exactly the noise it exists to remove.
- **`_spawn_bg(..., endless=True)` now makes the shape a property of the CALL SITE**, which is where it is known: endless -> a clean return is a WARNING; hand-off -> INFO naming it as expected. **A RAISE stays ERROR for both**, because a hand-off that throws never handed anything off — quieting the clean return must not quiet the fault (P248). **`endless` defaults to True**, so a new dispatch site that forgets the flag gets the LOUD treatment and the quiet one has to be asked for.
- **The positive half was under-reporting too, and the fix must not over-correct.** `bg: onchain_feed` alone reads as "the other two died". The heartbeat now appends `(+2 handed off)` — deliberately a COUNT of dispatches and never their names among the running list, because their inner tasks are owned by the child and this runner does not track them: listing them as alive would fabricate a liveness claim (P2/P223), the same defect as reporting a finished task as running.
- **VERIFIED LIVE after the deploy (P295b), on both halves:** the two hand-offs now read `[BG-TASK] sol_onchain handed off (its own inner tasks carry the loop from here) — expected, not a fault` at **INFO**, and the heartbeat reads **`bg: onchain_feed (+2 handed off)`** — the inline loop named as running, the two hand-offs counted and not claimed alive. Zero ERROR/CRITICAL, `HEALTH_STARTUP 11 PASS, 0 WARN, 0 CRITICAL`, and the 26 WARNING+ lines are the recorded benign startup set (P343). The FastRiskTick alerts that prompted this were re-checked and needed no change.
- **Mitigation pattern:** a mechanism that classifies events needs its taxonomy taken from what was already MEASURED about them, not from the shape the author has in mind — P356 had the endless/hand-off split written down one entry earlier, and the cost of ignoring it was an alert on the healthy path that only a live deploy could reveal. Deploying an observability change and reading its FIRST output is part of shipping it (P295b), because a test suite cannot tell you that a true statement is the wrong statement to make.

**PART 6 — [P357d] A THIRD PARTIAL COMMIT, AND THIS TIME THE MARKER WAS MINE AND SPELLED DIFFERENTLY.**
- `[P357b]` does not CONTAIN the substring `[P357]`. So `--marker "[P357]"` classified every sub-entry hunk as another session's and left it behind: the `_bg_handed_off` initialiser, the hand-off branch and the heartbeat segment all went missing, and **the committed tree failed four of its own tests while the working tree was green** — P311b for the third time in one entry.
- **The tool REPORTED it and I skimmed the tail.** The NOTE built one commit earlier listed those exact hunks under `[carries [P357b]]`; the output is long and I read the last four lines, which were the genuinely foreign `[P341b]` hunk. **A report that is correct and unread is worth what silence is worth** — and it is the second time in this entry that the mechanism found the defect before I did.
- **Fixed as the CLASS: a marker's base number is the campaign.** `[P357]` now matches `[P357]`, `[P357b]`, `[P357c]` — and deliberately not `[P35]`, `[P3570]` or `[P356]`, or isolating one entry would sweep a neighbour's. Suffixed sub-entries are this repo's normal way of recording a follow-up (P322b–f, P329b–d, P355b), so the base number is what "my changes" means; the alternative was remembering to pass the suffix, which is the affordance-versus-care trade this whole entry is about.
- **And one of my own tests broke on the fix, for a reason worth keeping:** it read the `endless` flag LINE BY LINE, and adding a marker comment split that call across two lines, so it reported the wrong shape for a correct call site. Re-expressed with `ast` against the CALL. A line-based scan of a multi-line call is a pin whose failure message describes the wrong defect (P320's character-window lesson, one syntax level up).

- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) when the same ambiguity costs four round trips in three entries, the defect is the missing affordance, not the author's care — and if a sibling tool already solved it, the fix is to port the concept rather than to be more careful a fifth time; (b) a scoping window's default is a claim about file geometry: verify it against a fixture with the REAL separation, because a fixture where everything fits inside the window cannot distinguish scoping from no scoping; (c) a probe that comes back VACUOUS is telling you the GUARD is thin — believe it after checking the probe (P238), because that is the only signal that distinguishes a test that passes from a test that would notice.

### P356. [DISARMED + AUDITED 2026-08-21, operator: "why the market is fluctuated, but there still no trade" -> "do both, and can you dig deeper"] The no-trade question decomposed — 75% is the book choosing flat BY DESIGN — then an async-lifecycle sweep, one real finding of four classes
Tests `tests/test_p356_disarm_and_async_audit.py` (13) + three older pins followed to their new decided values; nine falsification probes red-then-restored; full suite 6,104 green; gate clean, **zero baseline movement**, mypy unchanged at the standing 1084.
- **THE ANSWER, measured over 6 days and 336 asset-ticks — and it corrects the premise first: two of three assets are HOLDING** (`ETH +1.00 3ct`, `SOL +1.00 2ct`). There is no TURNOVER, not no position.
  | | BTC | ETH | SOL |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | book says **FLAT** | 68 | 81 | 103 |
  | holding **at target** | 25 | 5 | 5 |
  | **traded** | 17 | 3 | 3 |
  | **blocked** | 1 | **23** | 1 |
  **252 of 336 (75%) is the certified book choosing flat**, and the leg census says why: ETH `trend_flat` 39 / `trend_hold` 31, SOL `trend_flat` 65 / `hold` 8, BTC `funding_contrarian_short` 41 / `_long` 27 / `funding_short` 5. ETH's book is trend-only and SOL's hold-bull-only (P247/P250) — **"the market is fluctuating" is precisely the condition this mechanism sits out**, and P325 measured the expected turnover at ~6 round trips/year for ETH and ~13 for SOL. That low turnover is *why* fees stopped being the binding constraint (P315 had them at ~29% of the loss under the old ~442/yr trend seat).
- **AND THE ALPHA GATE'S 340 REFUSALS ARE MOSTLY NOT REFUSALS.** 70 are `est=0` — the book asserting no edge, so the gate is declining to trade nothing, not blocking a trade. Of the 270 real ones, **172 are at `est=10bps`** and 90 at 18, against thresholds of 26–54: that 10bps is the TREND seat's 2-of-3 vote, which P295 showed is untradeable by construction (its signal quantizes to 10 or 30 bps only). Only 4 rejections were at 30bps. So when the certified book is flat, a weaker fallback takes the seat and is correctly refused.
- **THE TWO ENTRY FILTERS DISARMED, by explicit operator instruction on that decomposition.** `coinbase_ma_filter_enforce` and `coinbase_whale_filter_enforce` -> **false**, annotated in the live profile with the reason and the one-line revert. The evidence has never distinguished either from noise in EITHER direction: P324 measured both NOT EARNED at the pre-committed bar once the t was overlap-corrected; P337, measuring against the decider they actually filter, found model_alpha's disagreements marked entries that did **BETTER** (contrast −10.0, t −0.72) and whale's marked no difference; P348 showed no obtainable sample makes it significant. **Both ledgers keep accruing with enforcement off** (P340 — the harness records the counterfactual either way), so the only thing given up is the blocking, and that is pinned by a test asserting the ledger write is not gated on the enforce flag. The decision FUNCTION is untouched, so re-arming is a one-line revert rather than a rebuild.
  - Three older pins moved with it rather than being relaxed — P236's, P298's roster and P293d's — each now asserting the NEW decided value, because the point of those tests was never the value but that nobody changes it quietly.
- **THE SWEEP: four mechanically-findable classes, none previously swept, and the clean results are worth as much as the finding.**
  | class | result |
  |---|---|
  | unawaited coroutines | **0 real** of 32 candidates |
  | blocking I/O inside `async def` | **0** in the engine (2 in an operator CLI) |
  | discarded background-task references | **1 real, latent — fixed** |
  | mutable default arguments (live path) | **2 — fixed** |
  | persisted-state schema drift | **0** (23 keys written, 23 read back) |
  The 32 unawaited candidates were all name collisions with sync methods (`self.exchange.fetch_open_orders` is ccxt's, not our async adapter's — `len()` on a coroutine would have raised) or coroutines appended to a list and star-unpacked into `gather`. Worth stating: the P293 per-tick feed driver, which the scanner flagged loudest, is correct.
- **THE REAL ONE: `asyncio.create_task(...)` whose Task is discarded, in seven places.** asyncio's own documentation: *"Save a reference to the result of this function, to avoid a task disappearing mid-execution"* — the loop keeps only a **WEAK** reference. Of the three background loops dispatched from `run_paper`/`run_live` it matters most for **`OnChainFeed.start()`, which runs its polling loop INLINE** (`while self._running: ... await sleep()`), so the Task **IS** the loop; the other two spawn tracked inner tasks and return, which makes their outer task safe to complete. The seventh is `_reconnect_position_sync` — a SHORT task, which is exactly the shape that can be collected before it runs, and if it is then positions are never re-synced after a reconnect.
  - **P37 FIXED EXACTLY THIS CLASS INSIDE `lead_lag_engine`** — its comment says so verbatim: *"Was discarded asyncio.create_task() result -> tasks could be GC'd mid-WebSocket loop"* — **and it was never applied to the call sites.** P171 for the BOM, P226 for the scanners, P323 for the timestamp, P355 for the entry-only guard, and now this: a mitigation applied to one instance of a class is not applied to the class, for the fifth recorded time.
  - **Reported as LATENT, not live, and the reason is stated rather than hedged:** the feed's loop logs only on error, so its silence is not evidence either way, and a task suspended on `asyncio.sleep` is generally kept alive by that future's callback chain. What justifies the fix is that the failure mode is documented, the fix is free, and the symptom it would produce — *"OnChainFeed... stay dormant -> dead signals (data_quality=0) for months"* — is written in the comment directly above the defect, describing the bug this same dispatch was added to fix.
- **The mutable defaults** (`def __init__(self, assets: List[str] = ['BTC','ETH','SOL'])`, twice in `lead_lag_engine`) are latent too — the shared list is stored on `self` and no mutation site exists today. Closed before one is written, and an explicitly-passed list is now COPIED, so a caller mutating their own list cannot change the monitor's universe underneath it.
- **A probe of mine was INVALID twice, both times for the same reason, and the harness was right:** the two classes have identical `__init__` signatures, so the anchor matched both. Re-anchored on the logger name that distinguishes them. Sibling ambiguity for the fourth time in three entries (P238/P349) — it is the single most common way a probe or a pin edits somewhere its author did not read.
- **What the disarm is expected to change, before it deploys:** ETH's 23 blocked ticks become tradeable, so expect ETH to enter when its book turns and model_alpha disagrees. Nothing else moves — the filters never touched exits, never force-exited a held position, and BTC/SOL had one block each in six days.
- **VERIFIED LIVE after the deploy:** both flags read **False** in-container; the `ma_filter` ledger is still writing (`reason: ma_disagrees_hold_kept`, `enforce: false`) — the evidence keeps accruing exactly as the disarm's justification requires; the three background loops are alive (`[SOL_ONCHAIN]` at a steady 2-minute cadence, so the now-referenced tasks are running); zero ERROR/CRITICAL; and `[NAV-LIVE] equity=$10,831.18 | peak=$10,838.93 | drawdown=0.07%` — P351's halt tracking a real drawdown against a peak that has survived three restarts.
- **What it does NOT change, stated because it is the larger half of the answer:** 75% of the quiet is the book, and the book's flatness IS the strategy. Trading the chop is a different mechanism, not a config flip — and P318 measured that at honest fees this book loses to buy-and-hold on RETURN while beating it on Sharpe and drawdown. It trades less on purpose. Building a chop-trading overlay without a measured basis is the P269/P283 mistake; the lab ladder (P262's protocol) is where that would start.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) "why no trade" decomposes into *the decider chose flat*, *the position is already correct*, and *something blocked it* — and only the third is a defect, so measure the split before touching anything; here it was 75/10/7 and the 7% was one asset; (b) a gate's refusal count is meaningless without splitting `est=0` (nothing to gate) from a real signal rejected — 21% of these "refusals" were the gate correctly declining to trade nothing; (c) when a fix's own comment says it was applied to one site, grep for the call sites — P37 fixed the task-reference class inside a module and left seven instances of it outside.

### P355. [FIXED 2026-08-20, operator: "can you make the ensemble regime classifier have input, and the anthropic cap has resolved"] Thirteen of the classifier's sixteen inputs existed all along under other names — and the resolved cap exposed a backoff that could not notice it
Two operator-facing items, and both turned out to be one shape twice: **a value that exists being read under a name nobody writes, and a date being trusted as a deadline when it was a floor.** Tests `tests/test_p355_classifier_inputs_and_quota_reprobe.py` (38) + four P329c/P345 tests re-expressed; eleven falsification probes red-then-restored; full suite 6,087 green; gate clean, **zero baseline movement**, mypy back to the tree's standing 1084.
- **1. THE CLASSIFIER'S INPUTS: 13 of 16 were recoverable, and 10 of those were a NAMING mismatch.** P347 measured 8 of its 10 market/technical inputs with no producer, so every `market_data.get(key, default)` returned the default on every tick — the model scored a market in which the price had not moved on any horizon, MACD was flat, Bollinger sat mid-band and CVD was zero. Re-measured against the producers, most of those quantities **are computed every tick, under a different name**:
  | classifier input | real producer | |
  |---|---|---|
  | `price_return_1h` | `price_change_1h_pct` | P306's real Kraken hourly |
  | `price_return_4h` | `price_change_4h_pct` | |
  | `rsi_14` | `rsi` | |
  | `macd_histogram` | `macd_hist` | |
  | `open_interest_change` | `oi_change_24h_pct` | |
  | `fear_greed_index` | `fear_greed_value` | |
  | `cvd` | `cvd_divergence` | **in `agent_signals`, not `market_data`** |
  | `price_return_24h` | 6 bars of 4H closes | derived |
  | `volatility_24h` | realized vol over the same closes | derived |
  | `bb_position` | `(close − bb_lower)/(bb_upper − bb_lower)` | derived |
  plus `volume_ratio`, `volatility_4h` and `funding_rate`, which were already correct. **Resolved at the READER**, where the mismatch is — not by publishing a second set of aliases into `market_data`, since a second name for one quantity is how the first one stops being read (P172).
- **THREE INPUTS HAVE NO SOURCE ANYWHERE AND ARE LEFT ABSENT, which is the half that keeps this honest.** `volatility_1h` needs an hourly price SERIES and the pipeline keeps only the last hourly CHANGE (P306); `basis` exists only inside the calbasis shadow ledger; `social_sentiment` has no producer at all. Inventing any of them would be indistinguishable from a measurement, which is the entire defect.
- **AND RESOLVING THE NAMES IS ONLY HALF THE FIX.** Without a refusal, a feed outage silently restores exactly the state P347 found. `_resolve_regime_inputs` now returns `(values, missing)` and the caller **REFUSES to classify** above a missing-count floor, saying which inputs are absent. An unusable value (None/NaN/inf/non-numeric) joins `missing` rather than coercing to 0 — the P2 rule at the one place it had been inverted sixteen times over. A roster test partitions the dataclass exactly, so a NEW `RegimeFeatures` field cannot be silently left to its default (P310's both-directions rule).
- **2. THE ENTRY-ONLY GUARD THAT COULD NOT WORK — and there were TWO of them.** `[V6 SHORT FILTER]` is flatten-intended, and its "is this a NEW short?" test read `position_state['current_exposure']`, which in LIVE resolves to the Kraken book — empty since 2026-06-13 (P275/P338). **Structurally true for every routed asset**, so the filter would have liquidated a live Coinbase short while believing there was none.
  - **The second one was found by a guard written for the first.** My test asserted `"if current_exposure >= 0:" not in src` over the whole file and caught `[P0 SHORT BLOCK]` — also flatten-intended, also entry-only by intent, one screen above, identical defect. **A mitigation applied to one instance of a class is not applied to the class** (P171 for the BOM, P226 for the scanners, P323 for the timestamp), and the only reason it surfaced is that the guard was scoped wider than the block it was about. Both now go through **one** `short_already_held()` — two copies is how two sites drift apart again.
  - **UNKNOWN is `None` and the callers test `is False`, never `not x`.** Firing a flatten-intended veto on an unreadable book liquidates a real position (P338's category error); not firing admits one short entry that every other gate still sees. A stale reconcile, a raising sleeve and a non-numeric exposure all read UNKNOWN, and each says so once.
  - **Worth recording while there:** `[P0 SHORT BLOCK]` *defers* to the V6 filter whenever the coordinator exists — and the V6 filter's classifier is not in the image, so `allow_new_short` keeps its default. Both shorts guards are therefore inert today, one because it deferred and the other because it cannot load. Deferring to a control that cannot run is the P152/P177 shape.
- **3. THE RESOLVED CAP EXPOSED A BACKOFF THAT COULD NOT NOTICE IT.** The Anthropic account cap stated a reset of **2026-09-01** and was resolved on **08-21**. `classify_external_failure` suppressed for the whole stated interval, so a long-lived process would have sat on the headline heuristic for **eleven more days**; Haiku is live now (`src=haiku status=live`, real headline counts) only because the hard-disable is in-memory and a restart wiped it. **A stated reset is the EARLIEST the vendor promises access back, not the latest** — the suppression is now the earlier of the stated reset and the bounded re-probe. **Capping only ever SHORTENS**, so P293b's real defect (a monthly quota retried on a 900s transient backoff, ~2,900 pointless requests) stays fixed at one request per re-probe interval, and the fail direction stays P319's: retry sooner than necessary, never go dark for weeks by mistake.
  - **This is P299's lesson un-applied.** P299 fixed exactly this for CryptoPanic — *"a backoff that encodes a date is encoding a guess about someone else's system; prefer a cheap periodic re-probe"* — and P329c/P345 re-created it for Haiku with the mitigating detail that the date came from the API rather than from us. The date being AUTHORITATIVE about when access returns is not the same as it being authoritative about when access returns **at the latest**, and that distinction is what cost the eleven days.
  - **Four tests pinned the assumption and were re-expressed, not relaxed.** They asserted "a server-stated reset must outlast the bounded re-probe". The invariant P319 was reaching for is that the server's date is **read and used, never replaced by a guess** — so a reset SOONER than the re-probe is still honoured exactly (pinned), a far-future one is capped with the stated interval named in the reason so an operator can see it was parsed, and neither may ever become "retry immediately".
- **A vacuous guard of my own, caught by its probe.** `test_the_caller_refuses_on_a_mostly_absent_vector` asserted `"_REGIME_MAX_ABSENT_INPUTS" in src`, which stays true under `if False and …` — the source-pin trap this repo has now hit four times (P234, P251, P307, here) and for which **P311 already built `assert_guard_live`**. Re-pinned through the helper, then re-probed red. The helper existed and I did not reach for it; that is the cost of the trap being cheap to re-create.
- **One mypy finding of mine, fixed at source rather than baselined:** the quota branch bound `secs` as `float` while the 429 branch below binds it `float | None` — one name, two types, the P342b shape. Renamed; back to the standing 1084 (P284b/P287g: never bake a finding into the baseline).
- **NOT SHIPPED, and pinned NOT shipped.** `training/regime` is still absent from `Dockerfile.engine` and `.dockerignore`, so none of this is live: the classifier cannot load, the short filter returns its default, and both guards stay inert. Arming it remains the operator's flip (P141/P347) — but the two reasons P347 gave for refusing are now gone: the inputs are real, and the guard can no longer liquidate a held short. A test fails if the module lands in the image, so that decision gets re-opened deliberately rather than arrived at as a side effect.
- **VERIFIED LIVE after the deploy:** zero ERROR/CRITICAL, `src=haiku status=live` on all three assets (the cap is genuinely resolved, not just restart-cleared), and — a confirmation of P351 two entries back — `[NAV-LIVE] equity=$10,833.86 | peak=$10,838.93 | drawdown=0.05%`: the peak SURVIVED the restart and the halt is now tracking a real, non-zero drawdown for the first time. Neither short guard fired, which is correct: nothing is directionally short and the V6 classifier is still not in the image.
- **[P355b — the tool that reports CI could not tell a transient failure from a permanent one, found while reporting THIS commit.]** Polling for `2cc3f58` returned `UNREADABLE: HTTP 504 from GitHub` and stopped — with fourteen minutes of budget left. P344 made `UNREADABLE` non-retryable on the argument that *"a 403 will not change inside the polling window and a 404 will never change at all"*: true of both, and **not true of a 5xx or a socket timeout**, which are facts about GitHub this second rather than about us. That is the same "I could not ask" / "no answer yet" conflation the tool was built to end, one class over — and the retry that resolved it thirty seconds later is the proof. New `TransientlyUnreadable` (a SUBCLASS, so it is still unreadable and can never be mistaken for GREEN) is raised for 5xx and network errors and retried within the same budget as PENDING; 403/404 stay terminal, pinned, because retrying those is the budget-burning loop P344 removed. An exhausted budget still returns UNREADABLE — a transient failure that never clears is not a pass.
  - **A vacuous guard of mine, caught by its probe:** the pin asserted `"return UNREADABLE"` within 700 characters of the transient handler, and the TERMINAL handler directly below returns the same string — so it stayed green when the transient path was changed to return PENDING. Scoped to the block it is about. Sibling ambiguity, for the third time in two entries (P238/P349), and the probe caught all three.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) before concluding a feature "has no data", check whether the quantity exists under a different NAME — ten of these sixteen did, and the fix was a rename rather than a producer; (b) an input roster must partition the consumer's fields exactly, or a new field joins by silently taking its default, which is the same defect one field at a time; (c) a vendor-stated reset is a lower bound on when access returns, so treating it as an upper bound converts every early resolution into weeks of self-inflicted downtime — bound every quota suppression by a re-probe you control.

### P354. [FIXED 2026-08-20, operator: "make a plan and do all remaining tasks"] The P353 windows, decided per accumulator on what each consumer's timescale actually is — two gated, two kept fast, and the split is the finding
P353 measured the defect and left the disposition open because "re-window everything" and "leave everything" are both wrong. Asked to finish it, the deciding question turned out not to be a risk preference at all: **two of the four accumulators have a train/serve CONTRACT and two have a consumer whose timescale is genuinely 30 seconds.** Tests `tests/test_p354_decision_cadence_gate.py` (11) + the P353 suite re-expressed; seven falsification probes red-then-restored; full suite 6,049 green; gate clean, **zero baseline movement**, mypy unchanged at the tree's standing 1084.
- **GATED to the decision tick, because the short window is a SKEW rather than a choice:**
  * **`_wavelet_buffers` (256).** P164 established that the causal wavelet must reproduce the training transform, which runs over **4H BARS** — so 256 samples is meant to be ~42 days and was **145 minutes**. This is the train/serve skew P214 fixed once for the missing module and nobody re-checked for the CADENCE. **P164's own parity guard could not have caught it**: `test_causal_matches_the_live_recurrence_exactly` pins the TRANSFORM and says nothing about what the deque is FED (P234's shape, inside a leak guard).
  * **RegimeSmoother `persistence=2`.** The Architecture Rules call it a train/runtime parity requirement, and in training it means **2 BARS**. At 34s it confirmed a regime change in **1.1 minutes** — ~424 advances between decisions, i.e. **no damping whatever at the horizon the rule is about**, which is exactly the ping-pong it exists to prevent. A non-decision call now SERVES the current smoothed label without moving the state machine, which is what a watchdog should see: the regime the decision was taken under.
- **LEFT on the 34-second feed, and this is a decision with a reason at the source, not an omission:**
  * **`_ofi_history` (42) -> `ofi_zscore` -> the SOL order-flow toxicity classifier.** Toxicity is a MICROSTRUCTURE property; a 24-minute window is the right horizon for it and the 7 days its maxlen implies plainly is not.
  * **`_depth_history` (120) -> `orderbook_depth` -> the execution TIMING score** (the `depth=` term in the `[PROOF]` line). "Is depth good right now relative to recent conditions" wants about an hour, not 20 days.
  Gating either would have been a preference with no evidence behind it, dressed as a correctness fix — the trap P353 flagged and this entry had to avoid while fixing the other half.
- **THE CLAIM THAT MADE THE GATE FREE, checked at the source rather than assumed:** `FastRiskTick.evaluate` reads exactly `current_price`, `data_valid`, `volatility_30m`, `orderbook_depth_1pct_usd` and `orderbook_stale` — **it consumes neither `regime_state` nor any `*_denoised` feature**, and its depth baseline is its own 4H anchor (P156), not the pipeline's median. So withholding the two bar-cadence appends costs the 30s watchdog nothing. Pinned by a test that fails if FastRiskTick ever starts reading one of the withheld keys, because at that moment the claim stops being true.
- **THE FAIL DIRECTION IS THE PART TO GET RIGHT, and it is deliberately the awkward one.** `for_decision` defaults to **False** everywhere, so a NEW caller cannot pollute a bar-cadence window by forgetting to opt out. The risk that buys is a decision site forgetting to opt IN — which starves the buffers silently — so **the decision sites are pinned by test rather than left to memory**: exactly two call sites may set it (`run_paper` and `run_live` each carry a near-identical prefetch block), a third would advance the smoother twice in one tick, and zero would starve every window. The watchdog call is pinned NOT to set it.
- **`core/execution_service.py`'s mid-decision re-read deliberately does not opt in** — it is a refresh within a tick, not a new bar, and passing True there would advance the smoother twice per decision. That is the same "exactly once per bar" property the call-site count pins.
- **P353's own guard fired on my fix and was right to** — that is the P318 anti-rot pattern working: its failure message says a gate IS the fix and that every window must be re-derived alongside it. **But it also revealed the guard was weaker than its docstring claimed**: the AST scan keys on the attribute name, and both the wavelet and depth buffers are appended through LOCAL ALIASES (`_wv_buf`, `_depth_buf`), so it could only ever have seen `_ofi_history`. Re-expressed as the positive statement it should always have been — *these two are ungated BY DECISION, and here is why* — which is both honest and the thing a future author actually needs.
- **One collateral repair: a P214 pin broke on a comment.** `test_the_wavelet_fallback_logs_a_warning` asserted `logger.warning` within **1200 characters** of the import, and the rationale comment for this gate pushed it past. The invariant was intact; the pin was fragile. Re-anchored on the `except` handler it is actually about — **a character-count window is a guard whose failure mode is a confusing message about the wrong defect**, which P320 recorded for the 5,000-char seat window and which silently penalises documenting a decision at its call site.
- **What changes live, stated before the deploy:** `regime_state` at the 4H tick becomes the label confirmed over **two decision ticks** instead of over the last ~68 seconds, so it is strictly more stable and matches what the models were trained on — it can suppress a genuine regime change for one tick, which is what `persistence=2` means. The five `*_denoised` features become a ~42-day causal window; their only consumers are the DRL observation builder and Exit-SAC, **both SHADOW**, so no live order changes and the effect is that both shadow IC streams stop being confounded. Nothing else moves.
- **VERIFIED LIVE after the deploy (P295b), on both halves of the split:** the UNGATED `_ofi_history` still turns over within 80 seconds on all three assets — so the execution-timescale buffers were not gated by accident — while `[NAV-LIVE] equity=$10,838.93 | peak=$10,838.93 | drawdown=0.00%` (P351 holding), zero ERROR/CRITICAL, and the book trading normally (`ETH=NOOP(3.0ct), SOL=OK(1.0ct)`). The 34-second watchdog cadence resumed unchanged after the boot tick — checked, because a first count over a window containing the ~2.5-minute boot tick read like the loop had slowed, and the timestamps say it had not. The gated half is structural and is carried by the tests and probes rather than by a two-minute observation; do not read the three constant regime labels since the deploy as evidence either way at n=3.
- **Evidence discontinuity:** shadow-IC readings for the DRL and Exit-SAC streams are not comparable across this deploy — before it the denoised features were computed over ~145 minutes of 34-second snapshots, after it over ~42 days of 4H bars. That is the P214 caveat resolved rather than restated, and the resolution is itself a boundary.
