- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) when one function serves two consumers on different clocks, the question is never "which cadence is right" but "which of its OUTPUTS has a contract" — here the answer split 2-2 and either uniform answer would have been half wrong; (b) a guard that scans for an attribute name cannot see an append through a local alias, so any "nothing is gated / everything is gated" claim built on one is narrower than it reads — say which names it can actually resolve; (c) the cheapest way to make a cadence claim safe is to pin the CALL SITES that may set the flag, because "exactly once per bar" is a property of the callers, not of the callee.

### P353. [MEASURED 2026-08-20, operator: "any remaining tasks"] Every rolling window in the pipeline is ~424x shorter than the bars its size implies — the 30s watchdog runs the FULL pipeline, and three earlier entries reasoned from the wrong cadence
Found by asking why the log showed a market-data fetch every ~34 seconds while the decision loop runs every 4H. Tests `tests/test_p353_pipeline_cadence.py` (12); six falsification probes red-then-restored. **Deliberately no behaviour change — see the disposition below.**
- **THE MECHANISM, and it is by design at the top and unintended at the bottom.** `run_live` sleeps to the next 4H candle **in 30-second chunks** so FastRiskTick can act between decisions (P110/P227) — correct. On every chunk it calls `self._prepare_market_data(frt_asset)` for all three assets, which is the **WHOLE pipeline**: Kraken OHLC, 1,000 trades for VPIN, Best-of-N selection, GMM inference. And `fetch_and_prepare` mutates its rolling accumulators on **every** call — **there is no `tick_count` gate anywhere.**
- **MEASURED over the retained logs — 2,541 full pipeline runs per asset per day against 6 decision ticks:**
  | asset | n | median gap | p90 | per day |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | BTC | 14,773 | **34.0s** | 34.0s | 2,541 |
  | ETH | 14,771 | 34.0s | 34.0s | 2,541 |
  | SOL | 14,774 | 34.0s | 34.0s | 2,541 |
  so every `maxlen` counts 34-second samples, not 4H bars:
  | buffer | maxlen | **actual window** | window its size implies |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `_ofi_history` | 42 | **23.8 min** | 7 days |
  | `_depth_history` | 120 | **68.0 min** | 20 days |
  | `_wavelet_buffers` | 256 | **145.1 min** | 42.7 days |
  | RegimeSmoother `persistence` | 2 | **1.1 min** | 8 hours |
- **Verified live rather than inferred:** the persisted `ofi_history` buffer's contents changed for **all three assets within 80 seconds**, between two 4H ticks, and `saved_ts` advanced 102s. It is also full at 42/42/42 two days after P316 shipped its persistence, where a 4H cadence would have produced ~15.
- **WHAT THIS FALSIFIES IN THIS FILE, which is the reason the entry is worth more than the fix:**
  * **P316 sized the OFI warmup at "~20 HOURS of uninterrupted uptime"** from "ONE sample per 4H tick", and P301/P302's persistence work rests on the same premise. **Five samples take 170 SECONDS.** The persistence those entries built is still worth having — it survives a deploy mid-window — but the clock they justified it with never existed.
  * **The Architecture Rule "RegimeSmoother persistence=2 must match training + runtime" is false at serve.** In training the persistence is 2 **bars**; here it is 2 x 34s, so by the time a 4H tick reads `regime_state` the smoother has advanced ~424 times and provides **no damping at the decision horizon at all** — precisely the ping-pong it was written to prevent. Measured: **52 suppressions across ~44,000 pipeline calls**, while BTC's GMM label spans five distinct regimes. Corrected in place in §Architecture Rules.
  * **P164's parity guard proves the wrong half.** `test_causal_matches_the_live_recurrence_exactly` shows the causal wavelet TRANSFORM reproduces the training one bar for bar — and says nothing about what the runtime deque is FED, which is 34-second snapshots. A guard that pins the function and not its input, inside the entry about a leak (P234's shape, in a leak guard).
- **BLAST RADIUS, traced at the consumers rather than assumed.** The five `*_denoised` features reach only the DRL observation builder and the Exit-SAC agent — **both SHADOW**, so no live order depends on them; what they confound is both shadow IC streams, which is the P214 caveat with a much larger cause. `ofi_zscore` reaches the SOL toxicity classifier; `_depth_history` feeds the depth median and the collapse detector **FastRiskTick itself alerts on** (the P240 `depth_drop=66-69%` burst came from this); and `regime_state` is consumed broadly and live — ADVISE weights, smart beta, the kraken_quant buckets, the trend gate.
- **DISPOSITION [SUPERSEDED by P354, which split it per accumulator rather than uniformly — the paragraph below is why a uniform answer was refused, and it still stands]: measured and recorded, NOT re-windowed — and the reason is not caution.** The four accumulators serve **two consumers with genuinely different cadence needs**: a 30-second watchdog that must see fresh depth and volatility, and a 4-hourly decision whose windows are specified in bars. Gating the appends to decision ticks restores every documented window and would simultaneously change the depth median the emergency watchdog compares against, the OFI z-score band feeding a live veto, and the regime label feeding half the ADVISE layer — in directions that are not uniformly "more correct" (a 7-day OFI z-score is arguably a worse microstructure signal than a 24-minute one, whatever the constant implies). **That is a design decision per accumulator, not a bugfix**, and it is the operator's (P141). What ships is the arithmetic, so nobody re-derives it wrongly for a fourth time.
- **The pins are written so the FIX moves the record rather than drifting from it** (the P318 anti-rot pattern): a test asserts the appends are currently UNGATED and its failure message says that a gate IS the P353 fix and that every window in this entry must be re-derived alongside it. The turnover numbers are **computed** from the sleep chunk and the maxlens rather than typed, so changing either goes red.
- **Also surfaced, not a defect but worth knowing:** the inter-tick watchdog loop exists **twice** — `run_paper` and `run_live` carry near-identical copies — which is why a probe anchored on the shared line matched two sites. The P353 pins read `inspect.getsource(run_live)` and are scoped correctly; a future edit to one copy and not the other is the standing hazard.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) a buffer's `maxlen` is a window only in the units of its FEED, so before quoting any rolling window in days, find every caller of the function that appends to it — here a 30-second safety loop silently re-defined four windows that three separate entries then reasoned about in bars; (b) when a component is documented as needing "N ticks", measure the actual inter-sample gap in the live log before building anything on that number — it is one `awk` over timestamps and it falsified two entries' arithmetic; (c) a parity guard must pin what the function is FED as well as what it computes, or it certifies the half that was never in doubt.

### P352. [FIXED 2026-08-20, operator: "instead of disarm, can we debug the code, to make those integrate"] Three gates acting on a number that describes something other than what it claims — including one whose magnitude had become the ACCOUNT BALANCE
Offered the choice of disarming the two armed entry filters, the operator asked for the integration to be debugged instead. Three defects were found by measurement, and they are one shape: **a gate acting on a quantity that is about the wrong subject.** Tests `tests/test_p352_filter_integration.py` (164); twelve falsification probes red-then-restored through the P328 harness; full suite 6,023 green; gate clean, **zero baseline movement**, zero mypy findings added in `risk/` or `defense/`.
- **1. THE LEDGER CLAIM'S MAGNITUDE WAS THE ACCOUNT'S CONTRACT SIZE — and it is the September read that was being corrupted.** `MAFilterEchoStrategy` sets `conf = min(1.0, abs(direction))` where `direction` is the sleeve TARGET. Until P274 `target_for` returned ±1, so that expression **was** a sign indicator; **P274 made the target equity-scaled and the claim silently became a magnitude.** Measured on the server's own ledgers, the scored `x = direction × confidence`:
  | family | BTC | ETH | SOL |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `ma_filtered` | {1, 2} | **{7, 8}** | {3} |
  | `whale_filtered` | {2} | **{7, 8}** | {3} |
  `compute_shadow_ic` scores x by **RANK** and **POOLS** both families across assets, and **P332 pre-committed the pooled read as the one that GOVERNS promote/kill** — so ETH's claims outranked SOL's outranked BTC's for no reason but sizing. The scorer's own docstring guards precisely this on the RETURN side (*"a high-volatility asset would otherwise occupy the extreme ranks"*) and **nobody guarded the SIGNAL side**. Worse, BTC's magnitude moved **1 → 2 as equity grew**, so the series was tracking the balance and changed definition mid-window.
  - **The fix belongs at the producer, and the census is what proves it:** of **30** shadow families on the volume these two are the **only** ones whose |x| ever exceeded 1.0. Every other family emits ≤ 1.0 by construction, so standardising in the scorer would have moved 28 innocent series to fix 2 (P299's discontinuity rule). The claim is now the SIGN with full confidence on a directional claim and 0 on a flat one — exactly what the P236-followup comment beside it already said — and the contract count is preserved as `diagnostics.ledger_target`.
- **2. THE WHALE VETO FIRED ON A "NET PRESSURE" COMPUTED FROM ONE TRADE.** P349 named this and left it, because gating on the count makes an ARMED filter fire LESS and that was the operator's call. It has now been made. Measured over every retained log — **118 bucket-hours, 1,233 detections**:
  | n whales | buckets | emits a direction | **\|p\| = 1.0 (saturated)** |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 27 | **100%** | **100%** |
  | 2 | 23 | 87% | 83% |
  | 3–4 | 18 | 89% | 61% |
  | 5–9 | 16 | 69% | 25% |
  | 10+ | 34 | 76% | 18% |
  and in 131 days of attribution **73% of all directional whale readings carry confidence exactly 1.000**. `whale_count` has been computed, stashed, and written to this very ledger since P349 — **and the decision function never received it**, because `sleeve_agent_filter_decision` takes a bare SIGN. Computed-but-unenforced (P144), on a live veto.
  - **The floor is 2 because that is the arithmetically FORCED number, not a fitted one:** with a single observation there is no "net" to take, so the ±0.3 deadband tests nothing and 100% of n=1 bucket-hours emit a full-conviction direction. Higher floors are progressively a risk preference (**n≥3 removes 47% of would-be vetoes, n≥5 removes 63%**) and the knob `coinbase_whale_filter_min_whales` is deliberately **ABSENT from the live profile** so the default governs and raising it stays an operator statement (P239).
  - **The fail direction is the load-bearing half.** P349 stashed an absent or unparseable count as **0**, which was harmless while nothing read it and is not harmless now: a producer gap would read as "zero whales", fail the minimum, and **silently disarm the veto**. UNKNOWN is now `None` — at the reset too, where 0 would mean "a completed count of zero" — and an unknown count keeps the veto **ARMED** while saying so once per asset. A missing field must never be the thing that switches a control off (P2).
  - **The gate can only ever REMOVE a veto, never create one**, pinned exhaustively over the position × target × direction grid, and the `evidence_ok` default is True so every existing caller — including the ma_filter wrapper — is byte-identical.
- **3. THE GAMBLER GATE JUDGED THE RETIRED DECIDER.** `strategy_agreement` is `abs(sum(signs))/4` over the Best-of-N TA indicators; since P298 the direction comes from the regimebook seat, which consults none of them. P346 measured the consequence on the gate's first firing in 50,676 ticks — an entry the alpha gate had passed at 66bps against 53. The fix is **P346's own mitigation pattern given a mechanism**: the pipeline now stamps `strategy_agreement_producer` beside the figure, and when that stamp disagrees with `primary_strategy` the clause is **NOT APPLICABLE** and is skipped rather than evaluated against a number about someone else. **Confidence and composite score, which ARE about the decider, still bind** — and a real agreement below its bar still blocks, pinned, so this cannot decay into a blanket loosening. An **absent** stamp keeps today's behaviour.
- **TWO HYPOTHESES CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, which is the half that keeps this from being three fixes and a guess.** (a) I expected `model_alpha`'s own confidence to be the ma_filter's integration defect. Measured: at its 295 disagreements confidence spans **0.341–0.619 (p50 0.465)** and **data_quality is 1.0 on every one of them**. So there is no dq defect, and a confidence floor would be a NEW hypothesis with no evidence — the ma_filter's decision rule is left exactly as P236's evidence built it. (b) 33 of 309 whale disagreements carry `data_quality = -1.0`, which looked like a second gate — until reading the producer: that is `DQ_NOT_REPORTED` (P265), an ATTRIBUTION-EXTRACTOR artifact about a missing key, not a statement about the reading. Gating on it would have been gating on the wrong subject, in the entry about gating on the wrong subject.
- **EVIDENCE DISCONTINUITY, recorded so nobody diffs across it:** `ma_filtered` and `whale_filtered` rows written before this deploy carry `direction` in CONTRACTS (±1…±8) and rows after carry a SIGN. **Per-asset** IC is unaffected in kind (a monotone transform within an asset) but not bit-identical, since equity-scaling made ETH's own magnitude move between 7 and 8; **pooled** IC changes materially, which is the fix. The September reads should be taken on post-P352 rows, or on pre-P274 rows, never on a window spanning both.
- **The ledger whitelist told me about my own new keys before the tests did** — P350's warn-once latch fired on `_maf_whale_min` / `_maf_whale_evidence_ok` exactly as designed, which is the first time that mechanism has caught a live author rather than a historical one.
- **VERIFIED LIVE on the first post-deploy tick (P295b), and the whale row is the defect firing in the wild:**
  ```
  whale_filtered  direction 1.0  confidence 1.0  reason "whale_low_evidence"
    whale_count 1   whale_pressure 1.0   whale_min_count 2   whale_evidence_ok false
    raw_target 6    ledger_target 6.0
  ma_filtered     direction 0.0  confidence 0.0  reason "ma_disagrees_hold_kept"
    raw_target 6    ledger_target 0.0
  ```
  **One whale, pressure exactly 1.0** — saturated by construction, precisely the n=1 case the table above measures at 100% — and the gate now says so instead of publishing a full-conviction direction. `direction` is **1.0 rather than 6.0** and a flat claim carries confidence **0.0**, so the pooled series no longer ranks by contract size and nothing saturates on a zero (P224). NAV also reads `equity=$10,819.29 | peak=$10,819.29 | drawdown=0.00%` (P351 holding), zero ERROR/CRITICAL since the deploy.
- **Not claimed: the ETH position is not this change's doing.** ETH entered **3 contracts at 22:37**, on the P351 deploy and BEFORE P352 shipped — model_alpha stopped contradicting it for one tick and the existing filter let it through. It is disagreeing again now (`ma_dir -1.0`), and the position is correctly HELD rather than force-exited, which is P236's v1 scope working as designed. Reporting it any other way would have credited a fix with a trade it did not cause.
- **[P352b — THE COMMIT WENT CI-RED, and the cause is a blind spot in the P350 tool I used to make it safe.]** `tools/isolate_commit.py` keeps only the hunks whose ADDED lines carry your marker, then verifies two things: your marker is present in the staged blob, and no FOREIGN marker appeared. **Both are true of a PARTIAL commit.** Two hunks of mine carried no marker — a function SIGNATURE line and a config PARSE line, whose explaining comments sat in NEIGHBOURING hunks — so they were dropped, the tool printed success, and HEAD went red with **142 failures** because every caller of the new kwarg hit a `TypeError`.
  - **Attributed the way P344 prescribes rather than guessed:** `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into scratch, run the suite there, and the missing symbols fall out in one command (`git show HEAD:main.py | grep -c "evidence_ok=True):"` → **0**). The working tree cannot tell you what you committed (P311b) — and here it was the *tool for committing* that could not either.
  - **The fix is that the tool now SHOWS instead of counting.** It prints every dropped hunk with its location and its added lines, and **REFUSES when a dropped hunk carries no marker of any kind** — precisely the ambiguous case, since a dropped hunk stamped with somebody else's P-number is attributable and passes quietly (refusing on those would fire on every shared-tree run and become wallpaper, P202). `--accept-unmarked` is the explicit escape for when you have read them and they are theirs. **"3 hunks do not carry your marker" was a COUNT, and a count is not a location** (P293b/P349) — that is the whole of the fix, and it is the third time this repo has learned that sentence.
  - Three further probes red-then-restored, including one that makes the refusal fire on ATTRIBUTABLE hunks too, so the guard cannot be "strengthened" into something everyone disables.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) when a signal's magnitude enters a RANKED, POOLED statistic, check what that magnitude is made of — here it was the account balance, and it had been for four days without any test noticing, because per-asset ranks were unchanged and only the pooled read moved; (b) "debug it rather than disarm it" is the more informative instruction: disarming would have ended three measurements, and debugging found that two of the three suspicions were right, one was wrong, and a fourth (dq) was about the wrong subject entirely; (c) a threshold that can be DERIVED from the arithmetic of the statistic (n=1 ⇒ the ratio is a constant) is worth far more than one fitted to the data it will act on — state the forced floor, measure what the looser ones would cost, and leave those to the operator.

### P351. [FIXED 2026-08-20, operator: "continue with remaining tasks"] The LIVE drawdown halt has NEVER been able to fire — the snapshot reads an equity that the only per-tick refresh will not write until later in the same tick
Found by reading the live WARNING sweep after a routine post-deploy check, not by any test. Fix in `main.py`; tests `tests/test_p351_nav_equity_freshness.py` (13); five falsification probes red-then-restored through the P328 harness.
- **THE MEASUREMENT, and it is 4 ticks out of 4 since the deploy:**
  ```
  [NAV] equity fetch failed (FAIL-CLOSED: Account equity unavailable.
        Status=VALID, Age=14326.6s, Equity=0.398431766369)
  [NAV] equity is the notional fallback ($20,812.98), not an exchange reading
  ```
  **`Status=VALID` is the tell: the state was not broken, it was OLD.** `AccountState.is_valid()` refuses above `MAX_EQUITY_AGE_SECONDS = 120`, and the age is **14,326s — one full 4H bar, ~120x the bound**, on every tick.
- **THE MECHANISM, provable from ordering alone.** `run_live`'s loop takes the drawdown snapshot at the TOP, then enters `for asset in self.config.assets`. The **only** per-tick `account_sync.refresh()` lives at the top of `_process_4h_tick_inner` — inside that loop. So the freshest equity available when the snapshot runs is always the PREVIOUS iteration's, and the read raises **structurally, forever**. It is not a venue outage and it cannot self-correct.
- **WHAT THAT COST, all of it silent.** `_equity_is_real` was never True, so **`_current_drawdown_pct` was never written**: the LIVE 25% halt (P201) could never compare anything, the regime-leverage de-risking ladder (`DD>12%` scale-down, `DD>22%` force 1x) and the DRL observation's `drawdown` dim read their `getattr` default **0.0** forever, and `[NAV-LIVE]` reported `initial_capital + sleeve` as though it were an exchange reading. **P163 fixed the missing WRITER of that field; the writer then became unreachable for a different reason** — the same control, disarmed twice, by two unrelated mechanisms.
- **The fingerprint that proves it rather than argues it:** `peak_equity` in the server's `paper_positions.json` is **0.0**. `_peak_equity` is assigned in exactly one place, past the `_equity_is_real` guard, so a persisted zero is the writer's own record that it has never run.
- **AND THE SNAPSHOT'S OWN COMMENT PREDICTED IT WOULD SELF-HEAL.** It says the halt "stays inert until account_sync has refreshed" — true about the FIRST tick of a process, false about every tick after it, because the refresh is permanently downstream of the read. **A comment that certifies a state as transient is a claim about ORDERING, and it stops being true the moment the two sites sit in the order it assumed away** (P261's shape: a comment certifying a path as safe, whose premise a change elsewhere silently invalidated).
- **The fix is one helper used by both loops (P172), not a second hand-rolled refresh** — two copies is exactly how paper and live diverged in the first place. `_refresh_equity_for_nav()` refreshes immediately above the snapshot in `run_live` AND `run_paper`. **It swallows every failure on purpose:** a refresh that fails leaves the snapshot behaving exactly as it does today (hold the last known drawdown, halt inert), which is the conservative direction, and it must never take the trading loop down.
- **PAPER was dead too, and differently — worth stating because it hid the live case.** With `_peak_equity` never set, the paper `[NAV]` line's direct `self._peak_equity` read raised `AttributeError` into a `logger.debug("[NAV] Snapshot failed")` swallow, so the whole paper NAV block was silently gone (P160). Two modes, one cause, neither visible.
- **EXPECTED LIVE EFFECT, stated before the deploy so it can be checked.** `_peak_equity` anchors at the FIRST real combined reading (Kraken **$0.40** + sleeve ≈ **$10.8k**), so the drawdown starts at 0 and **the halt cannot fire on arrival** — it only ratchets from there. The de-risking ladder becomes real, the DRL's `drawdown` dim stops being a constant (SHADOW, so no order changes), and `[NAV-LIVE]` should read **~$10,8xx instead of $20,812.98**. Every one of those is protective or observational; **there is no loosening in this change**, which is why it is a bugfix rather than a P141 arming — the operator's `risk.hard_drawdown_halt: 0.25` is declared, parsed and consumed, and has simply never had a number to compare against.
- **Checked rather than assumed, because an intermittent input here would be the P261 hazard on a THIRD equity feed:** Kraken equity is $0.40 because `crypto_assets = ('BTC','XBT','ETH','SOL')` — **XRP is not valued**, consistent with the P272/P273 decision that the ~$12.4k bag is unmanaged. So the bag cannot enter the peak one tick and leave it the next, which would read as a >50% drawdown and HALT. Three consecutive live readings (0.3958 / 0.3965 / 0.3984) confirm it is stable, not intermittent.
- **VERIFIED LIVE on the first post-deploy tick, which is the only evidence that counts (P295b):** `[NAV-LIVE] equity=$10,813.76 | peak=$10,813.76 | drawdown=0.00%`, **zero** `[NAV] equity fetch failed` lines, and `peak_equity` in the server's state file moved **0.0 -> 10813.76** — the writer that had never run in the process's life now runs and its value survives a restart. Every number matches the prediction above, including that the halt anchors at ~$10.8k rather than the fabricated $20,812.98 and cannot fire on arrival. The book was directional at the time (SOL long 1ct), so this was not an idle-book deploy.
- **Recorded, NOT fixed:** a per-asset ticker failure inside that valuation logs a warning and **silently drops that asset's value out of equity**. Negligible today against $0.40 of dust; a real partial-book hazard the moment Kraken holds size again.
- **The premise is pinned, not assumed.** A test fails if `MAX_EQUITY_AGE_SECONDS` is ever raised above a 4H bar — at which point the defect dissolves and so does the reason for the pre-snapshot refresh, and the next reader should re-derive it rather than inherit it.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) when a consumer reads a cached value with a freshness bound, check WHERE the producer runs relative to it — "there is a refresh every tick" is not "the value is fresh when I read it", and the gap is invisible because a stale read and a healthy zero produce the same downstream number; (b) a `getattr(self, X, <neutral>)` consumer cannot distinguish "never written" from "measured neutral", so any field guarded that way needs its WRITER checked for reachability, not just for existence — this is the second time the same field has been found unwritten in LIVE; (c) a persisted `0.0` for a high-water mark is a writer's confession, and it is cheaper to read than any amount of tracing.

### P350. [BUILT 2026-08-20, operator quoted the four residual items] Four lessons from P349, each given a mechanism — and building them exposed a limit in one of my own helpers
P349 recorded four things as prose and fixed each one instance-at-a-time. **A lesson recorded in prose is the thing this file exists to convert into a mechanism (P280/P328)**, and the same operator move (quote the paragraph back) produced P344 two entries ago. Tools `tools/isolate_commit.py`, helpers in `tests/_guard_pins.py`; tests `tests/test_p350_mechanisms.py` (22) + the P349 suite retrofitted onto the helpers; six falsification probes red-then-restored.
- **1. THE WHITELIST NOW REPORTS WHAT IT DROPS.** `MAFilterEchoStrategy`'s diagnostics dict names the keys it forwards, so an observation key the caller sends and it does not name never reaches the ledger — the P2 reader/writer shape **inside the harness built to observe**, and P349 lost two keys to it. Any `_maf_*` key the dict does not name is now reported **once per key** naming the file to edit. Warned, never raised: a ledger must not be able to break a live tick (Iron Law 7). Warn-ONCE rather than per-tick, or it becomes the wallpaper P202 is about.
- **2. `assert_text_pin` REFUSES AN AMBIGUOUS NEEDLE.** P349's reset pin asserted a substring the SET half's exception fallback also satisfies, so it stayed green with the reset deleted — **a count is not a location (P293b)**. The helper now treats an ambiguous needle as an ERROR: either scope it with a unique `near`, or use a needle that occurs once. **That refusal is the load-bearing half**, because the vacuous pin had no anchor at all.
  - **AND ITS OWN TEST CAUGHT A LIMIT I HAD IMPLIED AWAY.** I wrote the docstring as though `near` isolates the site; it does not — it anchors the SEARCH, and a sibling sitting inside the window still satisfies the pin. The deletion test failed on exactly that, on a fixture where both sites are 100 chars apart. Rather than loosen the test to fit, the limit is now stated in a **WHAT IT DOES NOT DO** section (the `assert_live_line` precedent), the default window is tightened 1500 → 400, and a test pins the failure mode so it cannot be forgotten. **A helper that overstates its guarantee is worse than none, because the next author stops looking.**
- **3. `assert_detector_is_precise` FORCES BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Over-broad detectors have now cost four rounds: P307 (prose containing "not"), P330 (`--` cutting the shell long flags it protected), P349 (a `hasattr` init read as a decision), and the first draft of P350's own reset test. The tempting fix is always to loosen until the author's case passes, which is how a real guard dies (P248). The helper takes `must_catch` and `must_not_catch` and **requires both non-empty** — recall is the direction that goes quiet, because a detector that stops firing reports clean and clean is what a healthy tree also reports (P174).
- **4. `tools/isolate_commit.py` — "my changes to this file" now has an implementation.** There is no incantation of add/commit that means that: `git add X && git commit` takes the whole INDEX (P314, and P311b pointing the other way), and `git commit -- X` takes the WORKING TREE, which holds the other session's uncommitted hunks (P304 and P314 both did this; P349 nearly did). The tool diffs against HEAD, keeps only the hunks whose **ADDED** lines carry your marker, and applies those with `git apply --cached`, which never touches the working tree. **The verification is the point**: it re-reads the staged blob and refuses when your marker is missing or when a marker appears that is neither yours nor already in HEAD. "I checked the diff looked fine" is what the previous eleven collisions all had. Deliberately NOT a committer — a tool that commits is one that eventually commits the wrong thing unattended.
  - Exercised against the real shared tree the day it shipped: on a `main.py` holding one of my hunks and one `[P341b]` hunk of the parallel session's, it reports **2 hunks, 1 carrying the marker**, and refuses outright on a marker nobody used.
- **The helpers are USED, not shipped beside the tests they were extracted from** (P170: a mechanism nothing calls is decoration) — the P349 suite now goes through `assert_text_pin` and `assert_detector_is_precise`, and its detector had to declare the two cases it must catch and the two it must not.
- **One finding of mine on the way, fixed at source rather than baselined:** the warn-once latch (`set()`) added a `var-annotated` finding in `defense/`, which IS in CRITICAL_DIRS. Annotated; mypy back to the 1084 that the parallel session's uncommitted work plus the P227 environment fingerprint account for, so this change adds **zero** (P284b/P287g — never bake a finding into the baseline to make a gate green).
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) when a fix is applied "one instance at a time" four times in one entry, the entry is a list of four missing mechanisms, not four fixes; (b) a helper's docstring is a CONTRACT, and the first test that fails against it is more likely telling you the contract was overstated than that the test is wrong — say what it cannot do, in the docstring, next to what it can; (c) the operator quoting your own paragraph back is a request for the mechanism behind it, and it has now produced P344 and P350 from prose that both times read as finished work.

### P349. [MEASURED + WIRED 2026-08-20, operator: "why whale needs threshold, isn't that monitor the big money move"] The ±0.3 is an AGREEMENT threshold, not a size one — and a threshold on a ratio cannot express "enough big money"
The question exposed a conflation between two different thresholds, and the measurement behind it is the finding. Observation-only wiring (nothing gates on the new field); tests `tests/test_p349_whale_sample_size.py` (12); five falsification probes red-then-restored.
- **YES, IT REALLY DOES WATCH BIG MONEY, and that test is sound.** `WhaleDetector.detect` requires **>= 2 of 3 dimensions**: >= **$100K** absolute, >= **10x that asset's own** average trade, >= **5%** of 1% book depth. The relative leg is per-asset since P265, because one global baseline suppressed detection on SOL and inflated it on BTC. Live detections look exactly like whales: ETH tickets of $110K-$355K, BTC $140K, each tagged with the dimensions that fired.
- **BUT THE ±0.3 IS NOT THAT TEST.** `net_pressure = (buy_vol − sell_vol) / (buy_vol + sell_vol)` over the whales found in the last hour — a RATIO in [−1, +1] saying which way the whales leaned, not how big they were. Some deadband is the right KIND of guard there: without one, a 51/49 split emits a full ±1.0 direction, a coin flip promoted to maximum conviction (the P224 saturation shape).
- **THE DEFECT: a ratio threshold screens BALANCED flow and cannot screen THIN flow.** With one whale `net_pressure` is exactly **±1.0**; with two on the same side, **±1.0**. Both clear ±0.3 trivially. Measured across every retained log — **2,597 detections in 123 (hour, asset) buckets: median 3 whales per bucket, min 1, max 415, and 53 of 123 buckets (43%) hold <= 2.** So nearly half the time the direction is mechanically full-conviction off one or two tickets.
- **The field that WOULD express it exists and nothing reads it.** `whale_count` is computed by the detector, returned on `WhalePressure`, published into `market_data` (:2089) AND `agent_signals` (:11588) — and consumed only by a log line and the "mixed" label. `whale_direction_from_pressure(net_pressure)` **takes one argument and it is not the count.** Computed but unenforced (P144/P170), on a signal that is currently ARMED as a live entry veto.
- **It also stops the measured noise being mysterious.** whale's own IC is 16h **t=0.26** (P293c) and P348 puts its disagree bucket at +1.9bps against agree +6.1 — indistinguishable from nothing. A signal that reads ±1.0 off a single $100K trade should look like that, and $100K is small against BTC's tape.
- **WHAT SHIPPED IS THE MEASUREMENT, NOT THE GATE.** `whale_count` and `whale_net_pressure` are stashed per-asset (reset at the top of the tick beside the direction reset — P155-L5/P294, or a ledger row carries the previous tick's sample size) and recorded in the `whale_filtered` ledger. **Nothing decides on them**, pinned by a guard that fails if any line ever compares the stash. Gating direction on a minimum count would make the ARMED filter fire LESS, i.e. a loosening, which is the operator's call (P141) — and P348 already says that filter has no measured basis to be armed at all.
- **The ledger's diagnostics dict is a WHITELIST, which the first draft did not notice.** Adding the keys at the call site alone left them silently dropped — the P2 reader/writer shape inside the harness built to observe. They are added at the producer, and **conditionally**, because `MAFilterEchoStrategy` is shared with the ma_filter (P294): an unconditional key would write a null into every ma_filter row, which reads as "measured zero whales" rather than "not applicable" — P2 again, one level down.
- **A vacuous guard of my own, caught by its probe.** The reset test asserted `"self._last_whale_counts[asset] = 0" in src` — and the SET half's exception fallback assigns the same text, so the assertion stayed GREEN with the reset deleted. **A count is not a location (P293b).** Re-pinned by POSITION (the count reset must sit within the block containing the direction reset it describes), then re-probed red. A second guard of mine was over-broad in the opposite direction — it flagged the `hasattr` initialisation as a "decision" — which is the third time this repo has made that mistake (P307 prose, P330's `--`); fixed by precision plus an anti-vacuity test that a real gate IS still detected.
- **Bounded, checked rather than assumed:** dedup runs first in `detect()` and correctly skips a repeated `trade_id`, but `_is_duplicate` returns False when the venue omits an id, so those trades are re-counted on every overlapping fetch. At a 4H cadence the 1-hour pressure window makes that harmless; on a day with several restarts inside one hour (today had ~4) the same trades can re-enter the window and inflate both count and pressure.
- **Shared-tree note:** `main.py` carried a parallel session's uncommitted `[P341b]` hunk. A pathspec commit takes the WORKING TREE, so it would have swept their work (P314) — this landed instead by building the blob from `HEAD:main.py` plus only the three `[P349]` hunks, staging it with `hash-object`/`update-index`, and committing the index. Verified before commit: 3 `P349` markers staged, **0** `P341b`.
- **Mitigation pattern:** when a signal is a RATIO, the threshold on it answers "which way" and can never answer "how much evidence" — those need two different guards, and the second one is the one that gets forgotten because the first one looks like a filter. Check what the denominator is made of before trusting any normalised score.

### P348. [MEASURED 2026-08-20, operator: "can we use existing data to make the judgement"] Yes — and the answer is that ALL the data is already in, the filters are NOT EARNED, and the September read I kept citing as "the settle" is a clock that cannot fire
The operator asked whether the entry-filter question could be decided from data we already hold rather than waiting. Decomposing the inputs the P296 way answers it, and the answer corrects my own standing plan, which I had restated three times this session.
- **THE DATA IS ALREADY EXHAUSTED, and here is the inventory rather than an assertion.** Attribution spans **2026-04-07 -> 08-20, 131 files, 3,091 rows** — `model_alpha` present in all 3,091 and **directional in 885** (ETH 321 / SOL 314 / BTC 250), `whale` present 2,482 / directional 872. The decider is recomputed from price+funding over six years (P337). Joined: **464**. Running the review at a 200-day window — i.e. everything that exists — returns the same verdict as at 90: **NOT_EARNED for both**, and there is no further input to add.
- **THE ARITHMETIC THAT SETTLES THE WAITING QUESTION.** t scales as sqrt(n), so from the observed statistics:
  | statistic | now | at the ~09-07 read | n needed for \|t\|>=2 | calendar |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | model_alpha contrast h1 | t=0.73 (n=67) | **t=0.79** | 503 | **2.8 years** |
  | model_alpha contrast h4 | t=0.14 (n=61) | ~0.15 | 12,449 | 75 years |
  | whale contrast h1 | t=0.37 (n=105) | **t=0.40** | 3,068 | **10.8 years** |
  | whale disagree h1 | t=0.24 (n=105) | ~0.26 | 7,292 | 25.7 years |

With gambler quiet the check is SKIPPED ENTIRELY and there is no veto. So entering gambler/OPPORTUNITY mode does not merely change sizing; it **adds a veto opportunity that does not otherwise exist**, and on its first ever firing that is exactly what it did. ### P345. [ROOT-CAUSE 2026-08-20, operator: "can you do root cause fixes"] The transient-vs-structural question had no home — five recorded incidents, five different wrong answers, ~12 sites re-deriving it
Asked for root causes rather than instances, the strongest candidate had five recorded instances and one missing abstraction. New `infra/failure_policy.py`; tests `tests/test_p345_failure_policy.py` (19); four falsification probes red-then-restored, **one per incident**.
- **THE CLASS, and its five wrong answers.** Every external-API caller must decide *is this failure transient or structural, and until when do we stop calling?* Each site answers it from scratch:
  | | what happened | what it should have been |
  |---|---|---|
  | P293b | a MONTHLY quota retried on a 900s transient backoff — ~2,900 pointless requests | structural, dated |
  | P319 | the backoff persisted as a GUESS about the vendor's billing cycle — fails ~19 days/month | bounded re-probe |
  | P329 | a transient READ failure took a 30-minute structural backoff, disarming an emergency watchdog for 23 min during a real 7% move | **no suppression at all** |
  | P329b | transient timeouts logged at ERROR forever — 9 of 10 lines, none actionable | warn, escalate on streak |
  | P329c | a hard-dated cap matched NEITHER the non-retryable list NOR the 429 branch, so it fell to a bare warning with **no backoff** | structural until the stated reset |
  Five instances, five *different* directions of error. That is the signature of a missing abstraction rather than carelessness.
- **THE FIRST THING I FOUND WAS A HELPER THAT ALREADY EXISTED AND HAD NEVER BEEN CALLED.** `infra/classified_retry.py` was written for this family — its own docstring names the failure mode — and `grep` returns **zero callers**. But reading it settles that it would not have prevented any of the five: it codifies **INTRA-call** retry (sleep, retry, N attempts inside one call), while every bug above is **INTER-call suppression** consulted on a later tick. Different axis. Both facts are recorded in the new module's header so the next reader does not wire the wrong helper and conclude the class is covered.
- **The contract, one clause per incident:** TRANSIENT **never suppresses** (`retry_after_sec is None`, deliberately distinct from `0.0`, which a caller would turn into a timestamp of *now*); RATE_LIMITED honours the server's stated interval; QUOTA_EXHAUSTED suppresses until the reset **the server named**, falling back to a bounded re-probe when it names none; PERMANENT suppresses for the process. **Quota is matched on the MESSAGE before the status**, because a dated cap arrives on 400 *and* on 429 — which is exactly how P329c fell through every branch. Severity tracks what an operator can DO (P202/P240).
- **The fail direction is pinned:** an unrecognised failure classifies **TRANSIENT**. Going dark by mistake is worse than one wasted call, and that is the direction P293b recorded after the opposite choice cost a month of coverage.
- **ADOPTED, not shipped as decoration.** A second uncalled helper would have been the joke writing itself, so the module's first caller is my own P329c code, which hand-rolled this logic *and* carried a private copy of the date parser. `_classify_haiku_error` now delegates; the caller reads a cooldown in seconds instead of re-parsing a date out of a reason string; **`_parse_regain_utc` is deleted** (P172: one implementation). Parity verified against the live incident end to end — 400 → non-retryable, cooldown 11.7 days to the stated reset — and every other class byte-identical, including the invariant that an ORDINARY malformed 400 is still **not** silenced.
- **The anti-decoration guard was VACUOUS on its first run**, which is the P174 shape inside the guard written to prevent decoration. It scanned for the substring `failure_policy` and matched `stop_order_failure_policy`, an unrelated config field in `main.py` and `execution_manager.py` — so it reported two callers when there were none. Tightened to match an actual import; it then failed correctly until adoption landed.
- **Two P329c tests had to be rewritten rather than relaxed.** They pinned the old `until=<date>` reason format and a `total_seconds()` source string that moved into the new module — a stale pin asserting the absence of relocated code. Replaced with a **producer/consumer contract test** (P310): the classifier's reason is round-tripped through the caller's own extraction, for both a stated and an unstated reset, asserting the stated one outlasts the bounded default. Stronger than either source pin.
- **Honest scope.** ~12 sites hand-roll this; **one** is adopted. The rest are working, untouched live feeds, and rewiring them for tidiness is the risk P141 exists to prevent — so they are named as the adoption surface rather than converted. What this buys is that the *next* site has somewhere to look, and that the five clauses above are now executable rather than remembered.
