### P307. [MEASURED + RESOLVED 2026-08-18, operator: "resolve this, and validate nothing is default on instead of off"] The duplicated GMM input was not free — it double-weighted `return_4h` and shifted a third of every asset's regime assignments, and my own P306 note said the opposite
Tests `tests/test_p307_gmm_and_defaults.py` (15); 7 falsification probes red-then-restored; full suite 5,173 passing; gate clean. Probe: `training/scripts/gmm_redundancy_probe.py`, report `training/reports/gmm_redundancy_probe_p307.json`.
- **THE CORRECTION TO P306, AND IT IS THE WHOLE ENTRY.** P306 recorded `ret_1h = ret_4h / 4.0` as a deliberate keep — train and serve agree, so parity holds — and added that "being exactly `ret_4h/4` it is perfectly collinear with `ret_4h`, so the GMM runs on 9 independent inputs, not 12", i.e. harmless. **The first half is right and the second half is wrong.** After the StandardScaler the two columns are IDENTICAL, and in a **full-covariance** GMM an identical column is not a no-op: the covariance is singular in that plane (regularised by `reg_covar=1e-2`) and the `return_4h` direction is counted **TWICE** in the Mahalanobis distance that assigns every bar to a cluster. "Carries no information" and "costs nothing" are different claims, and I asserted the second from the first.
- **MEASURED, with the production recipe** (same scaler, same `GMM_BASE_CONFIG`, same k=3..8 BIC search with the 2% minimum-regime rule, same split-aware fit boundary), refitting under three feature sets:
  | asset | ret1h≡ret4h/4 | corr | k (12) | k (11) | **ARI full vs no-dup** |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | BTC | True | 1.0 | 6 | **7** | **0.690** |
  | ETH | True | 1.0 | 7 | 7 | **0.657** |
  | SOL | True | 1.0 | 7 | 7 | **0.741** |
  Roughly a third of bar-to-regime assignments differ, and on BTC the duplicate changed BIC's **model-order** choice. **Honesty note carried in the probe: BIC is NOT comparable across these variants** — a different feature count is a different likelihood space, so the 12-feature fit reporting a lower BIC says nothing about which model is better; the discriminating statistic is the ARI, not the BIC.
- **RESOLVED by removing three inputs, not by making `ret_1h` real.** Dropped: `return_1h` (the duplicate), `cross_asset_correlation` and `spread_percentile` (per-asset CONSTANTS on both sides, P221 — zero variance, contributing no likelihood but an extra BIC-penalty dimension, which is what moved SOL's k). **The alternative — feeding the real Kraken hourly return P306 built — was rejected: it would make a network fetch a REQUIRED input to the live regime classifier, so an outage would break classification.** Removing a distortion adds no failure mode; adding a dependency does.
- **Executed as ONE P215 set**: both builders (`training/scripts/rebuild_pipeline.py` and `data_mgmt/market_data_pipeline.py`), the parquets, and the fitted artifacts moved in a single step. **Result: all three assets now select k=8** (was 6/7/7), the census is far more balanced (no cluster above 34%, against the old two-clusters-93% saturation), and `regime_confidence` softens to ~0.88. **`NEUTRAL_DRIFT` and `MOMENTUM_RALLY` exist in all three vocabularies again** — which retires the P306 note that "NEUTRAL_DRIFT does not exist in ANY clean vocabulary" and makes the previously-unreachable kraken_quant BULL bucket reachable.
- **The old artifact carried its own evidence, visible in the shipped JSON**: coordinates 0 and 1 of every deployed cluster mean were bit-identical (`-0.5857913130009003` twice on BTC). A test now fails if any deployed mean regains a duplicated coordinate pair — the tell is cheaper to check than the cause.
- **THE TREND-GATE VERDICT WAS RE-DERIVED, NOT CARRIED OVER**, because the refit changed the labels the lab reads. It gets **stronger**: the live gate set is negative in both eras on all three assets (**BTC −0.699 / −0.289, ETH −0.243 / −0.228, SOL −0.623 / −0.258**), now covering 27–40% of bars with NEUTRAL_DRIFT genuinely present. Both reports are kept (`trend_gate_lab_p306.json` pre-refit, `_p307.json` post-refit); do not diff across them without saying which labels each used.
- **A half-moved P215 set is now LOUD instead of silent.** A mismatched artifact/builder pair used to surface as a numpy broadcast error inside a broad handler — i.e. as a quiet fallback to the ADX proxy, exactly the state a partial deploy leaves behind. It now refuses with both shapes named. **The predicate is a module-level pure function because the first falsification probe of the guard stayed GREEN against `if False and ...`** — a pin on source text proves the code was written, not that it runs (P234/P251, third sighting).
- **THE DEFAULT-ON AUDIT.** 37 boolean `ProductionConfig` fields: 17 default TRUE, and 16 of those are ABSENT from the live profile (so they run on their code default). Widening to the whole tree found **87** `enable_*` / `*_enabled` / `use_*` dataclass switches defaulting True. Triage: the 13-strong `profit_max_*` family is the P287 finding and its vetoes remain classified sleeve-HOLD (pinned); everything else has a reader and was classified BINDS-SLEEVE vs KRAKEN-ONLY in P275. **Seven have NO reader anywhere in the tree** — switches that look armed and control nothing (P177): `use_birdeye`, `use_solscan`, `enable_proof_logs`, `proof_log_enabled`, `alert_popup_enabled`, `use_vol_percentile_adjustment`, and — the one that matters — **`defense/trade_gate.use_maker_fee`**, on a component that DOES bind the sleeve, reading as "the gate prices maker fills" when the gate always prices the taker fee. Annotated at source rather than deleted (removing a config field is a contract change), and the roster is guarded both ways: an EIGHTH fake switch fails, and an entry that gains a reader fails too, so it cannot become a parking spot.
- **THE LIVENESS AUDIT found one real defect.** Live `[AGENT-TRACE]`: BTC 7 of 16 agents directional, ETH 4, SOL 1 — with `flow` and `options` emitting for the first time (P298's netflow + Deribit PCR replacing structural zeros). Every `HEALTH_S*` check PASSes; the only WARNINGs are the micro warmup (persistence shipped P302, needs uptime), the cosmetic HF-Hub notice, and `[TREND-LAYER] +0.00` — which is correct, since BTC's direction now comes from the restored regimebook seat, not from trend. **The defect: `soldex` emitted `dir=+0.00 conf=1.00` on SOL.** Confidence was the raw liquidity score, independent of direction, so a deeply liquid DEX with NO arbitrage opportunity published a maximally-confident non-signal — and both fusion and the IC scorer consume `direction x confidence`. **This is the P224 defect verbatim, in a second agent.** Fixed the same way: confidence collapses to 0 on a flat direction, with the undiluted liquidity reading still available as `soldex_liquidity_score`.
- **Evidence discontinuities, recorded so nobody diffs across them:** every `regime`, `regime_proba_*` and `regime_confidence` value in the parquets changes definition at this refit, so the DRL shadow stream (P214's caveat, again) and any lab reading `_ctx` regime labels are not comparable across it. The regimebook shadow is UNAFFECTED — it uses its own causal SMA200 + funding labels, not the GMM.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) "carries no information" and "costs nothing" are different claims — a perfectly collinear feature is redundant in an information sense and still re-weights the geometry any distance-based model uses, so measure the effect instead of reasoning from the redundancy; (b) when a fix would restore a feature's *value*, ask first whether it would also add a *dependency* — removing a distortion is strictly safer than feeding a live model from the network; (c) a falsification probe that leaves the asserted substring in place (`if False and ...`) tests nothing, so any guard worth pinning belongs in a function the test can CALL.

### P293. [AUDITED + FIXED 2026-08-17, operator: "check macro / big-money flow / market emotion … then repair all + do we need new sources"] Three signal families audited; macro was dead through THREE independent paths, all by the same mechanism — a consumer wired to a cache no producer ever fills — and the answer to "new sources?" is NO for four of five gaps

Net: `macro_leverage_cap` a constant 1.0 — macro constrained nothing. **FLOW:** `exchange_flow` sums `raw["exchange_flows"]`, a list no configured source populates, so it is a **structural 0.0** and `flow_direction` (ADVISE weight 0.20) has been pinned at 0 for the life of the system; the one live component (tape whale detector, BTC +1.00/0.64) is one of the 12 deliberately zero-weighted agents (P228). **SENTIMENT:** L1 real and fusion-consumed; L3/Haiku dead (`headlines=0` — CryptoPanic 429 + CC quota 90/90); LunarCrush dead by the same no-producer bug; options PCR pinned at 1.0 (P218's 404s).
- **The sharpest finding — the one live signal of the three is miscalibrated.** `market_data["sentiment_zscore"]` is **not a z-score**: it is `(fg-50)/50*3`, a fixed linear rescale, because the feed asks for `limit=1`. Fusion derives the agent's confidence as `min(|z|/3,1)`, so a hardcoded scale sets the strength of a live ADVISE input. The same free endpoint serves **3116 daily rows back to 2018-02-01**. At today's F&G=31 the linear form says **z=-1.14 (confidently bearish, conf 0.38, emitted on all three assets every tick)** while the real trailing-365d distribution says **z=+0.25, 71st percentile** — the past year averaged ~27, so 31 is *above* average.

Two additions are free and keyless: **Deribit** (782 BTC / 654 ETH option instruments + DVOL) and alternative.me history. Deliberately NOT added: yfinance (a fragile scraper reaching worse data than the official API we already authenticate to), a replacement news feed (P228 records llm_sentiment sign-flipping between windows = noise; fix the billing before buying), Trading Economics. **The one purchase that might be justified — SOL exchange flow / options (CryptoQuant/Glassnode, ~$30-100/mo) — is explicitly deferred:** buying data for a signal that has not yet cleared P166 on the assets we CAN measure is the P269 mistake.

- **[P293e/f/g — operator: "build the contrarian variant / if everything is off and never promoted why bother / validate we fetch APIs efficiently, research it"] The "why bother" question measured, and the answer is a defect nobody had converted into the right units.**
  - **e — THE SENTIMENT EXAM (built, observation-only).** `defense/sentiment_variant_shadow.py` records three competing F&G readings per tick to `sentvariant_{ASSET}.jsonl`, judged by the SAME P166 gate: `sent_momentum_linear` (the live rule), `sent_momentum_hist` (same rule on the real historical z), `sent_contrarian` (the deterministic engine's own asymmetric mapping). Verified they genuinely disagree — **at F&G=80 momentum says +1 BULLISH and contrarian says −1 BEARISH.** The contrarian variant is deliberately NOT `-momentum`: a pure negation has an IC exactly the negative and would add zero information; the recorded claim is the engine's ASYMMETRIC mapping (greed penalised hard, extreme fear → **neutral, not bullish**), pinned by a test that fails if it ever becomes a mirror image. Prefix registered at both scorer sites with `ma_filter` still last (the P236 end-anchor, P248 lesson).
  - **g — WHY NOTHING PROMOTES: the 30-day clock CANNOT FIRE at 16h.** Measured: of 41 config gates, 15 are decided in the live profile and **11 are ON** — so "everything is off" is half wrong. But every promoted item is EXECUTION / COST / RISK (maker-first, reprice, venue-aware fees/funding/spreads/hold, routing, gated intent, fast-risk, flip-persistence, trend enforce), **never alpha** — because their evidence is ARITHMETIC (a maker fill costs 0 vs 3bps; no 30-day window needed). The alpha side is where the defect is. The gate needs `|t| = IC·sqrt(n_eff−1) ≥ 2` with `n_eff = n/h`, so at 6 bars/day: **a 30-day window can only certify IC ≥ 0.302 at 16h, while the ECONOMIC bar asks ~0.13 — the statistical bar is ~2.3× stricter, and an economically-adequate candidate needs ~330 DAYS.** The best live IC ever observed (0.048) would need ~3 years. **So the ~14 candidates on 30-day clocks against 16h horizons are on clocks that structurally cannot fire — a CHECK THAT CANNOT PASS, the exact inverse of P174's check-that-cannot-fail, and a defect by the same reasoning.** It hid because the gate reported its requirement in SAMPLES (`n_required~=1980`) and nobody converted it: the blocker line now reads `= ~330d of 4H bars vs ~30d held`. At 4h the arithmetic is fine (economic bar binds, ~27 days suffices) — the defect is horizon-specific, which is exactly why the gate must state it per horizon. **Recommendation recorded: stop adding alpha shadows until the clock question is settled** (lengthen to 6-12 months, or judge those claims at 4h, or pool assets to raise n) — a fourteenth costs maintenance and cannot produce a verdict sooner than the thirteen already running.
  - **f — API EFFICIENCY, researched then fixed.** Probed every dependency's response headers: **only RSS exposes validators** (`last-modified` + `s-maxage=300`); alternative.me, CoinGlass and Deribit return no ETag, no Last-Modified (Deribit says `no-store`) and **no rate-limit headers at all** — which is why client-side quota accounting (P220) is the only way to know where we stand. So conditional requests are available on exactly one source, and TTL-matched-to-update-cadence is the lever everywhere else. Waste found and fixed: **CoinGlass (PAID) had NO throttle on `fetch()` while the tick calls it once per ASSET and `_fetch_real` already loops all three symbols internally across 3 endpoint families — ~3× the requests needed**; **F&G is a DAILY value whose outer staleness check reads the DATA timestamp (so it is stale on every asset) and was refetched per asset**. Both now use `fetch_if_stale()`. RSS got a real conditional GET — **verified 4× `304` on the second fetch with the corpus intact** (a 304 REUSES that source's items; returning `[]` would read as "this source went silent"). `cache_age_seconds()` now has ONE definition instead of a sixth hand-rolled copy, handling datetime and float-epoch stamps with the P40/P97 naive/aware defence. Recorded as already-correct so nobody "fixes" it again: CC News serves all three assets in one request (P219), the CC budget is account-wide and persisted (P220), and every throttle survives restart (P293b); the remaining per-symbol loops are INSIDE one throttled fetch and are inherent — those APIs have no multi-symbol endpoint.
  - Tests: `tests/test_p293e_sentiment_and_efficiency.py` (28); 6 falsification probes all red. One test bug caught: selecting the feed class by NAME picked dataclasses (`FREDObservation`) — rewritten to select by CAPABILITY (the class that owns `fetch`), which also makes it catch any future feed that gains `fetch()` without a throttle. Zero baseline movement (one coercion refusal `noqa`'d at source).
  - **Mitigation pattern:** a promotion gate states its requirement in whatever units its arithmetic produces, and if nobody converts them the requirement is invisible — `n_required~=1980` and "~330 days" are the same fact, but only one of them tells you the 30-day clock beside it is theatre. Report thresholds in the units of the DECISION (calendar time), not of the computation (samples). And before assuming a caching problem, probe for `ETag`/`Last-Modified`: the textbook fix is unavailable on most JSON APIs, which changes the answer from "conditional requests" to "TTL matched to the data's update cadence, plus one fetch serving all assets".
- **[P293h/i — operator: "do we really need the tripwire, the 14 shadow clocks, and the 30-day contrarian exam"] Two of the three were answerable immediately, and the question surfaced a live-money reporting bug plus a coupling nobody had noticed.**

Now: bounded flow detection (a step exceeding max(≈$200, 0.5×position notional) cannot be PnL on a few nano contracts), excluded from PnL, **percentage rebased on invested capital** (start + net flows) so the ratio stays comparable, `external_flow_usd` recorded on every row so the adjustment is auditable, and the accumulator **persisted** (without it a restart re-books the transfer as profit — the P154 class). Fail direction deliberate: an ambiguous step stays classified as PnL — the honest-but-noisy reading — never a silent adjustment that could hide a real loss.
  - **i — THE CONTRARIAN EXAM WAS SUPERSEDED BEFORE IT COLLECTED A RECORD.** A 30-day forward exam was the wrong instrument for a question 6 years of data already answers: the F&G history is 3,116 days and price history is on disk. So the LIVE `main.py:7338` momentum reading is correct and `deterministic_sentiment.py`'s contrarian mapping is the one that must never be promoted. Honest caveat recorded: alternative.me builds F&G partly FROM price (volatility 25% + momentum/volume 25%), so this settles WHICH INTERPRETATION to use, not that F&G is independent alpha.

It fires on **30.8% of days** historically (**171 extreme-fear days in the last 365, zero extreme-greed**), and is dormant today ONLY because `trend_following_mode: enforce` overwrites `quant_direction` after the pipeline computes it. **So removing the trend injection does NOT take the book flat — it hands the wheel to Best-of-N, whose weights are modulated by a never-validated rule, in a regime where it fires ~47% of days.** Anyone firing the tripwire must decide what takes over FIRST.
  - **Mitigation pattern:** before scheduling a forward exam, check whether the question is answerable from history you already hold — a 30-day clock is the most expensive way to answer something a 30-second backtest settles, and here the historical data (3,116 days) had just been added by the same batch that proposed the wait. And when a decision "turns something off", trace what becomes the decider in its absence: an override can be the only thing keeping an unvalidated path dormant.
- **[P293j — ARMED 2026-08-17, operator: "the key issue is that we build the system that does no trade… let the whale turn on"] The no-trade cause measured, the tripwire DECIDED (delegated), and the whale seat armed — because whale's BINARY encoding is what clears the alpha gate that trend's fractional signal cannot.**
  - **THE NO-TRADE CAUSE, measured (the CLAUDE.md Trade-Frequency rule applied, belatedly):** ~7 order events across both retained logs; every tick summary reads `dir=+0.00` on all three assets and the gate logs `Alpha 10bps` against thresholds of 19-60bps. **The binding constraint is SIGNAL STRENGTH, not the tripwire:** trend emits |dir|≈0.33 → `40 × 0.33 × 0.75 = 10bps`, below every threshold, so the book sits flat.   - **WHY WHALE FIXES IT, and the honest caveat:** whale emits **±1.0 BINARY**, so it asserts the full 30bps whenever it speaks — clearing all three thresholds. Measured firing rate over 60d of attribution: **BTC 54% / ETH 43% / SOL 12%** of ticks directional, and whale speaks when trend cannot on **30% / 25% / 11%**. **Whale clears the gate because it is BINARY, not because it is better evidenced** — its live IC is +0.040 (4h) / +0.011 (16h), statistically indistinguishable from zero. It is however better than the INCUMBENT quant's **negative −0.046** at 16h, so the swap is defensible on relative grounds. Armed by explicit operator instruction, deliberately trading "no trades at all" for "trades on a weak but positive signal"; flip-persistence (2 ticks), the alpha gate, caps, stops and halts all still bind.

As written, a whale inside its ±0.3 deadband would have **seated 0.0 and forced the book flat on 46/57/88% of ticks**, which is both a churn engine and the P2 error (absence read as a position), and would have destroyed the fallback that drives those ticks. Fixed: a silent whale does NOT take the seat; the incumbent stands. **Copying a seat pattern without checking the new signal's SPARSITY is the trap.**
  - **THE TRIPWIRE DECISION (delegated by the operator, made here): DO NOT FIRE IT NOW.** The evidence for trend having no edge is strong (16h IC −0.046, calibrator 2/2 GATE-CLOSED on all three, −$225 realized over 65d). **But firing it does not take the book flat — it hands the wheel to Best-of-N, whose strategy weights are modulated by `[SENT-SWITCH]`, an unvalidated F&G rule that fires on ~47% of days in the current regime (P293i).** Removing a measured-weak signal into an unmeasured one is worse, not better. With whale seated, trend's practical role is already near-nil (it is blocked at 10bps on most ticks), so the tripwire's intent is satisfied in effect without activating the unvalidated path. **Re-scoped: at the 09-01 date the comparison should be whale-seat forward results vs trend, not a blind removal into Best-of-N.**
  - **Process note worth keeping:** the first config edit rewrote the whole `live_high_risk.json` via `json.dumps(indent=2)` — 160 insertions, and `0.10` silently became `0.1`, which tripped the authority scanner's drift check. Reverted and re-applied as a **3-line surgical insert**. A config rewrite is never a formatting-neutral operation; edit the text, not the parsed object.
### P295. [INSPECTED + BUILT 2026-08-18, operator: "inspect if our regimebook and trend setup right, and build the seat controller"] The trend signal is a 3-vote quantization that can only assert 10bps or 30bps — so it trades ONLY on unanimity — and the seat controller replaces the tripwire's kill-only shape
- **TREND INSPECTION — the precise mechanism of "the system does no trade".** `TrendFollowingStrategy.compute` is a VOTE: `sig += 1 if mom>0 else -1` over `lookbacks_days=(10,20,40)`, then `sig /= 3`. So **`sig` is quantized to {±1/3, ±1} — nothing in between.** Through the live alpha assertion (`40 × |sig| × 0.75`) that is **10bps (2-of-3 vote) or 30bps (unanimous)**, against live thresholds of 19.1/26.7/29.0. **A 2-of-3 majority is therefore untradeable BY CONSTRUCTION, and trend trades only when all three lookbacks agree.** Not a bug — but it is the exact reason the tick summaries read `dir=+0.00` with `Alpha 10bps` while the signal is never actually flat.
- **And a P174-class dead control found beside it: `min_abs_signal = 0.30` can NEVER fire.** It zeroes `|sig| < 0.30`, but the smallest reachable `|sig|` is 1/3 = 0.3333. The "weak trend → flat" branch is unreachable, so **trend always has an opinion**; it is the GATE, not the strategy, that produces the flat book. Pinned, including a guard that a floor rising above 1/3 would be a live behaviour change rather than a tidy-up.
- **REGIMEBOOK INSPECTION — one candidate is fine, one is correct-but-idle, one is structurally dead.** BTC `v1_full` works, but over 71 ticks **every in-market tick came from its FUNDING legs** (funding_short 14, funding_contrarian_short 6, flat 51) and **zero from its trend leg** — and P262 records the BTC funding legs as the **UNCERTIFIED** slice of that book, so seating BTC regimebook today would trade precisely the part that was never certified. ETH `v1_full` is `trend_flat` on 71/71 — **correct, not broken**: it is a trend-only book (P247) and the regime window held no bull (peace 37 / bear 34). SOL is `v1_degraded_no_bear_leg` on 71/71 because **P250 DELETED `configs/regimebook/SOL_bear_ridge.json`** (it was the leak artifact) and `configs/regimebook/` does not exist at all — so SOL's book is permanently inert and must be treated as UNAVAILABLE, never as "a candidate that says flat".
- **SEAT CONTROLLER BUILT** (`analytics/seat/seat_controller.py` + `scripts/seat_check.py`, 30 tests, 6 falsification probes all red). Replaces the tripwire's shape — one variable, one threshold, one direction, whose entire action space is "trade less" and therefore cannot serve a goal of trading. Design rules, each with its reason: **multi-variable** (the literature's requirement); **weakest-horizon scoring** `min(ic_4h, ic_16h)` so a candidate must be non-negative on BOTH (this system's signals repeatedly look fine at 4h and go negative at 16h — P198, P293k); **hysteresis** (a challenger must clear the incumbent by 0.02 IC, else the seat thrashes on noise — the flip-persistence argument, and Gârleanu-Pedersen's partial-adjustment result); **significance floor** (|t| ≥ 1.0 on the decisive horizon — every IC here sits inside noise, so without it the controller chases random ordering weekly); **UNAVAILABLE ≠ FLAT** (the SOL case — scoring a broken candidate as a flat opinion lets it win by default, P2); and **it never edits config** (P141 — prints the exact edit, exits 3). `flat` is an implicit candidate with score 0.0, so **the tripwire's verdict is subsumed as one outcome reached by comparison** rather than by a single-variable threshold.
- **It independently reproduces the P293j decision on the real 90d numbers:** whale +0.0110 is the only candidate positive on both horizons; trend scores −0.046; regimebook is unscoreable. Winner: whale, HOLD. Each recommendation carries its winner's structural caveat in the OUTPUT (whale clears the gate because it is BINARY, not because it is better evidenced), so the caveat cannot be lost by living only in a doc.
- **[P295b — HOTFIX, same day, caught by reading the live log after deploy] The P295 wiring passed `min_abs_signal` to the singleton FACTORY, which did not accept it.** Every tick raised `TypeError: get_trend_decision_layer() got an unexpected keyword argument`, main.py's handler logged `[TREND-LAYER] process skip`, and **the trend layer produced NOTHING at all** — inert in the opposite direction from intended. It failed SAFE (no signal rather than a wrong one, and the whale seat still held the slot) but the control was not doing what the commit said. **The P295 test pinned the CALL SITE as a source string, which proves the argument is PASSED and says nothing about whether the callee accepts it — P234 verbatim, committed by the author quoting P234 two paragraphs earlier.** Fixed on the factory (and applied to an already-built singleton, or a config change would reach only a cold process); now covered by a test that CALLS the factory, plus a signature check that every kwarg main.py passes exists on it. **Mitigation pattern: verifying a deploy means reading the live log for the thing you changed, not checking the container came up healthy — this was invisible in `docker ps`, in the test suite, and in the CI gate, and visible in one grep of the first tick.**
- **[P295c — the tool could not run where its evidence lives.]** `scripts/` is excluded from the engine image by `.dockerignore` (the P141 allowlist: `scripts/` also holds `launch_live.py`/`coinbase_test_order.py`/`coinbase_flatten.py`, and order-placing code must not be baked into the live trading container). So `docker exec ... scripts/seat_check.py` failed with "No such file or directory" — a weekly decision tool shipped somewhere it cannot work, the P213 shape. Added to **BOTH** halves (Dockerfile COPY **and** a `.dockerignore` negation), which is the P192 rule: naming a file in the build recipe is not putting it in the build context, and one half alone makes the image unbuildable. The blanket exclusion stays. Now scheduled Mondays **06:40 UTC** (after all five existing evidence jobs), via a wrapper that resolves the NEWEST timestamped report at run time and **exits 2 when no report exists** — "no report" must never read as "flat wins".
- **[P295d — the first live run recommended vacating every seat on n=0 evidence. Two defects, and the second is the one that matters.]** (1) **Parser shape:** `agent_ic_review` emits `agents.<name>.horizons.<h>`; the reader read `agents.<name>.<h>`, so every agent parsed to `{}`, every candidate fell below the evidence floor, and the verdict was computed from nothing — **registered-but-unreadable, P264 verbatim**, and caught only because the tool was finally run against real producer output. (2) **The aggregate hole:** `decide_seat` asked "is any candidate positive?" without first asking "is any candidate SCOREABLE?", so with zero scoreable candidates **flat won by default** — the module's own rule 5 forbids exactly this one level down (UNAVAILABLE ≠ flat, so a broken candidate cannot win by default), and **the set-level version of that per-item rule is a different code path, which mine did not obey.** Now a distinct `refused` outcome: incumbent holds, no config edit printed, exit 2. **Flat may only win by COMPARISON** — at least one candidate measured and found non-positive.
- **[P295d — what the real evidence says, now that it can be read]** (30d, 2026-08-17 report): `quant` (the seat's own series) IC 4h **−0.0326** (t −0.87, n=713) / 16h **−0.086** (t −1.14, n=704) → score −0.086; `whale` 4h **−0.0698** (t −1.05, n=226) / 16h **−0.0651** (t −0.48, n=225) → score −0.070. Both scoreable, both negative on both horizons ⇒ **flat wins by comparison** (exit 3, a real verdict). **Two caveats travel with it and must not be dropped: the whale series over that window measures whale as an ADVISE agent, not as the seat it took on 2026-08-17, and quant's series is pre-P295 trend (the 10bps votes the gate vetoed).** Neither is evidence about the configuration now running — **the first honest read of the CURRENT book is the 2026-08-24 report.** The recommendation was deliberately NOT applied (P141).
- **Mitigation pattern:** a decision tool's first run against **real producer output** is part of shipping it, not a follow-up — this one was verdict-complete, fully tested, and wrong in the direction that recommends flattening a live book. And when a module states a rule about one entity, check the AGGREGATE obeys it too.
- **Mitigation pattern:** when a signal "never trades", inspect its RANGE before its logic — a vote over N lookbacks is quantized to N+1 values, and if the gate threshold falls between two of them the strategy is not weak, it is *unreachable*. And a floor constant (`min_abs_signal`) is only meaningful if the guarded quantity can actually land inside it; check the reachable set, not the comparison.
- **Mitigation pattern:** when several consumers of one datum all read neutral values, do not go looking for N bugs — check whether the datum has a PRODUCER at all. `grep` for `.fetch(`/`.start(` on the feed, not for readers of it. Three independent macro paths here died of the identical cause, and each had been "verified" by someone reading a consumer. And any accessor named `get_*` that returns a populated dict on an empty cache makes absence unfalsifiable: give it a provenance sibling, or the status flag is a constant wearing a measurement's name. **[P293b addendum]** Two more, both earned the hard way: (a) **an API's own error body outranks your arithmetic about its quota** — I reasoned from request-rate to "this cannot be a limit" and the endpoint said the opposite in plain text, so probe the vendor before writing off a whole class of cause; and (b) **a rate limiter is only as durable as the clock it reads** — persisting a backoff while leaving the throttle timestamp in RAM protects the rare case and leaves the common one (restart) uncovered, which is how a monthly budget disappears in nine days.

### P278. [VALIDATED 2026-08-16] The retrain question re-examined under maker economics — verdict NO retrain now, but the cost-bar arithmetic found a REAL crossing with a dated, free-to-measure re-entry condition
Operator asked to validate whether the derivatives work needs a retrain. Verdict from the recorded evidence + one new measurement:
- **Nothing that killed the model families has changed.** The 0/39-fold verdicts (TQC ×3 campaigns, supervised zoo, meta-labeling, banded, pooled — P200/P241/P249/P250/P258/P259b/P263) died on CHURN BEHAVIOR, ERA-FRAGILITY and DIRECTION QUALITY as much as on cost — none of those is touched by anything shipped since. The P258 re-entry rule stands: RL only with a new formulation premise. The clean GMM deploy (P267) explicitly did not void the retrains; the breadth assets stay DELIBERATELY UNFITTED (fitting them burns the P262 virgin-evidence property that certified the trend mechanism).
- **The one genuinely new fact: maker economics MOVE THE COST BAR ACROSS THE MEASURED SIGNAL.** Every campaign priced 3bps taker (6bps RT). The P166 required-IC at 16h (σ=107bps, 2× margin): RT 6bps → **IC 0.134** (the bar every probe failed); RT 3bps (half-maker mix) → **IC 0.067**; RT ~1bps → 0.022. The strict edge-probe ICs (BTC 0.089 / ETH ~0.08 / SOL ~0.09 at 16h) sit BELOW the taker bar and **ABOVE the half-maker bar** — the settled "signal below the cost of trading it" verdict is CONDITIONAL on a fee regime that P270 just changed.
- **Why this still does not justify a retrain TODAY:** the crossing is conditional on the maker FILL RATE, which is unmeasured (n=1 live attempt, 0 fills, thin weekend book). Retraining before the effective RT is measured would repeat P269's mistake in reverse — GPU spent on assumed economics. The fill-rate evidence is FREE: every sleeve order logs `[COINBASE-MAKER]` filled-vs-fallback.
- **The dated re-entry condition (recorded so it cannot be re-derived or forgotten):** after ~2-4 weeks of maker ledger evidence, compute the effective RT (maker_fills×~0.5bps + taker_falls×6bps weighted). **IF effective RT ≤ ~3bps: the justified move is the SUPERVISED revival, not RL** — re-fit ridge_a30-class on the clean parquets (the exact P254-recorded revival path: "re-fit + re-certification on the clean parquets first"), judged at the MEASURED cost, through Rung-3 shadow. RL stays dead regardless (behavioral/era failures are fee-independent — P263c measured BTC losing GROSS even where its IC held). The P166 gate itself stays at 6bps×2 until the fill rate is measured — overcharging is the safe direction (P167).
- **Mitigation pattern:** a "no edge after costs" verdict is a joint claim about the signal AND the fee regime — when the fee regime changes materially, re-run the bar arithmetic before re-running any training. Here the arithmetic cost nothing and converted "retrain? no, never" into "no — until a specific free measurement lands, then supervised-only, at the measured cost".

- **The one live change: `coinbase_venue_aware_funding: true`.** P218 built it and proved it inert on the DIRECTION consumers — but the coverage audit surfaced what P218 missed: the alpha gate's hold-cost arithmetic (`FrictionComponents.update_funding_rate` → `_margin_cost_bps`) charges whatever rate `market_data` carries, so with the flag OFF the sleeve's hold cost was priced on KRAKEN's funding. Now routed assets charge the venue that holds the position (~1bp today — small, honest, tightening-direction; wrong-way failure keeps Kraken's rate).
- **Coverage verdict now on record:** every taxonomy family with strong-or-moderate evidence at this scale is live or examined; the rationally-skipped set (options/VRP, delta-neutral carry, sub-minute lead-lag, dated-futures spreads AS TRADES) is skipped with the evidence cited; sentiment remains deliberately over-built and zero-weighted. **Twelve candidates now sit P166 exams** (regimebook raw/adj, derivflow twins, ma_filter, volskip, etfflow, breadth books, + the five P277 families).
- **Mitigation pattern:** "implement everything" is compatible with discipline exactly one way — every addition enters as a ledger with its evidence grade written on it, and the ones the literature couldn't certify (oidiv, calbasis, xsmom) are precisely the ones where the forward exam IS the first real evidence anywhere. And when a falsification probe stays green twice in one batch, the probe is auditing the TEST — check what branch the fixture actually reaches, and what regime (contango vs backwardation) the fixture's numbers actually encode.

### P274. [BUILT 2026-08-16, operator-instructed] Equity-scaled sizing — the idle-$7k decision made executable: a deposit now deploys itself under the standing caps, with zero behavior change until the money actually moves
Operator: "we should use the idle $7k kraken usd." The wire itself is physically the operator's (Kraken → Coinbase → perp portfolio; steps below); what the SYSTEM owed was that arriving capital gets USED — the P273 fixed {1,3,1} contract book would have left a doubled sleeve at ~0.15× net, recreating at the new equity the exact under-utilization P273 fixed at the old one. Tests +5 in `tests/test_p272_advisory_and_caps.py` (24; two load-bearing pins falsification-probed red).
- **Mechanism:** `coinbase_target_fraction_by_asset` (P201 trio + ctor; live `{BTC:.15, ETH:.15, SOL:.15}`) → `_sized_contracts(asset)` = floor(fraction × `sleeve_equity_usd()` / 1-contract notional). **ONE function is both the target and the per-asset contract cap** (cap == target at any equity, P172 single-source) — without the cap following the size, can_trade's fixed {1,3,1} caps would block the scaled targets the moment capital arrived (caught at design time; pinned). Ctor clamps fractions to ≤0.25 (the largest standing P210 per-asset cap — a fat-fingered 1.5 must not size a 10× book).
- **The activation-safety identity, pinned by test:** at the activation equity ($3,775), 0.15 fractions reproduce the P273 book **exactly** ({BTC:1, ETH:3, SOL:1}) — behavior is byte-identical until capital moves; at ~$10.9k the same config yields {BTC:2, ETH:8, SOL:4} ≈ 0.45× max net, still under the 0.50 net cap and every P210 fraction cap, all of which are equity-denominated and scale automatically.
- **Fail-safe direction:** unreadable equity or an unpriceable contract → `None` → the FIXED contract book (sizing is never fabricated from missing data, P2/P208; staleness resolves toward the smaller known-safe book — including in can_trade, where an unpriceable tick binds the FIXED cap).
- **The operator transfer (recorded; only they can execute):** Kraken: buy USDC with the USD → withdraw USDC to the Coinbase USDC deposit address (minutes, ~$1 network fee; ACH via bank is the slow alternative) → in Coinbase, move the funds from spot into the **perpetuals/derivatives portfolio** (the sleeve reads CFM portfolio equity). The system needs NO config change on arrival — the next `snapshot()` reads the new equity and the next managed tick sizes to it. Equity-feed effects are benign by construction: P0 combined equity RISES (a deposit reads as a gain against the anchors — conservative direction; the fuse window sees a positive delta once).
- **Mitigation pattern:** a "use the capital" instruction has two halves — the wire (theirs) and the elasticity (ours). Fixed-size configs are correct exactly once; any sizing decision expressed in absolute units silently expires the day the denominator changes. Express policy in fractions, derive units at the edge, and pin the identity that makes the switch a no-op at the current state.

- **Mitigation pattern:** the probe-first discipline paid three times in one batch — post_only enforcement (which made the maker ladder safe to build), the ETF endpoint's real path (v3 404s, v4 serves), and the reporting-lag caveat (which demoted a +6.5-Sharpe backtest to a hypothesis and let the forward ledger be the judge). And when a mechanism FAILS a lab (P256's volfilter), record which FORM failed — the winning form here was the same idea on the opposite tail, entry-gated instead of position-gated.

### P269. [FIXED 2026-08-15] The docs-vs-implementation cross-check ("fix all") — the canonical training commands trained the WRONG formulation, a second undocumented live GMM was overwriting the calibrated posterior, and a latent fallback classified assets with another asset's model

All fixed, pinned by `tests/test_p269_crosscheck_fixes.py` (19; six load-bearing pins falsification-probed red — after first catching my probe harness itself running under an interpreter with no pytest, rc=1 reading as "red": the P159 shape INSIDE the falsification tooling; probes re-run under `sys.executable` with green-before-probe asserted):
- **1. Every scripted DRL entry point trained the retired formulation.** `make drl` and `run_training.run_drl` both lacked `--decision-interval 4` (training the every-bar churn design three campaigns measured dead, P242/P258), and the Makefile additionally forced `--lr 3e-5` + `--buffer-size 2000000` (pre-Optuna lr; the buffer the Stage-9.7 fix capped) with a FIXED tag `makefile_default` — whose second run would restore cached folds and report stale numbers as if it trained (P200 gotcha). CLAUDE.md's own Training Commands section carried the bare no-flag command. All now carry the full honest-flag set with per-run fresh tags.
- **2. The 500K buffer cap only existed under `--config`.** The cap sat inside `if args.config:`, so any plain CLI `--buffer-size` (exactly what the Makefile passed) flowed uncapped into the model. Moved out; unconditional.
- **3. A SECOND live GMM nobody documented was overwriting `regime_confidence`.** `market/regime_navigator.py` carries an ONLINE-FIT 6-component GMM (legacy STRONG_* vocabulary), and main.py:~7750 let its confidence max-overwrite the per-asset GMM's calibrated posterior in both signal dicts — two classifiers' confidences silently fused under one key, partially defeating the P267 deploy's calibrated ~0.90-0.92 posteriors (any tick the online GMM was more confident, a saturated old-style number won). The overwrite's own comment claimed it "wires into the alpha gate" — regime confidence is not on the gate path at all. RETIRED; the navigator keeps its namespaced `p0_regime`/`p0_regime_confidence` keys.
- **4. Latent cross-asset model application.** main.py's loader sets the "legacy fallback" GMM fields from the FIRST loaded per-asset model (BTC), and `_predict_gmm_regime`'s else-branch reads them — so an asset whose artifact pair went missing would be silently classified with BTC's GMM and BTC's regime names. Added (+0.08 bias, matching its 3.7%-of-ticks mild-bull census); `NEUTRAL_DRIFT` kept at 0.0 for old-parquet runs.
- **6. Docs corrected at the claim level:** TRAINING_GUIDE_V2 §2's phantom "convert 4h → _1d (see P200 session notes)" step replaced with the real fetchers (`fetch_binance_funding.py` + the P266 merge note) — no converter ever existed and the referenced notes are not in the repo; §5 "runtime hardcodes 1008" corrected (accepts 126/139 stacked, P241-P1b); §7 Rung-3 now states the two glossed-over mechanics (BEST_FOLDS hardcoded fold_3 in THREE files with no tag-aware loader, and the P215 atomic GMM+checkpoint deploy); Part4 v10 + training/README.md + README_V4.md got historical banners (Part4's header still claimed "DRL now DECIDE"); UNIFIED's Best-of-N regime-multiplier table corrected (code INVERTED it 2026-04-22: momentum in MOMENTUM_RALLY is ×0.7 not ×1.3) and its k=8 rows annotated to the clean k=6/7/7; METHODOLOGY_BRIEF gained the funding-rule reconciliation note (the regimebook funding legs are the rule's own "until forward data" test, not a violation).
- **Also:** `run_training`'s gmm step repointed train_per_asset_gmm.py → `scripts/rebuild_pipeline.py` (a standalone GMM refit against existing parquets breaks P215's one-versioned-set rule; the rebuild fits GMMs + regenerates parquets in one run) — the P189 orchestrator test updated to pin the new contract.
- **Mitigation pattern:** the canonical command block in the project's own instructions file is a deploy surface — it was three flags behind the guide it sat next to, and anyone (including a future session) following it would have burned a GPU-day re-measuring a settled verdict with the wrong economics. When a doc names a procedure, pin the COMMAND'S load-bearing flags with a test, not just the prose.

The scorer's price series was bounded by the MONTHLY archives (up to ~31d behind), so the ~09-07..09 P166 forward reads — the September exams — could only join through ~Aug-31. The extension fetches completed days only (today never fetched: its file doesn't exist and its day is incomplete — the P253c in-progress-bar class), re-fetches the boundary day (dedup keep-last makes the seam impossible), refuses gaps >62d (run the monthly fetcher instead of hammering zips), and degrades loudly to monthly-only on any failure. The TRAINING parquet is deliberately never touched (P199's separation stands). **Validated live: coverage 07-31 → 08-13 20:00 (0.5d behind now), and the overlap parity property held exactly — 13,095/13,095 bars vs the training parquet at 0.0 diff.**

- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) an archive fed from a bounded-depth API is the ONLY store of that history — its fetcher must merge, never overwrite, and its staleness must be surfaced where the operator already looks (`make check`), because the loss mode is silent and permanent; (b) freshness is a property of COVERAGE, not file mtime; (c) when a standing rule documents a two-step footgun (P253c), the durable fix is making it one step, not remembering harder.

### P261. [FIXED 2026-08-10 + KILL SWITCH RESET] The phantom −$3,776.44 kill switch — a restart's first tick fed the P0 controller a partial book against combined-denominated persisted anchors
- **The incident (2026-08-11 00:09:19 UTC, operator-reported from Discord):** `[KILL-SWITCH] max_daily_loss, Drawdown=34.76%, Daily P&L=-3776.44` — on a book that was FLAT and healthy. The "daily loss" is the sleeve's entire equity to the cent: the persisted P253 daily anchor ($10,865.13, combined) minus Kraken-only equity ($7,088.69). No real dollar moved; a ±1-nano-contract book cannot lose $3.7k in a day.
- **Mechanism — three individually-correct pieces interacting:** (a) P253 correctly PERSISTED the controller peak and daily anchor (so restarts don't forgive losses) at combined denomination; (b) the sleeve object is built lazily by run_live's heartbeat AFTER the first tick, so a fresh process's first `pre_tick_update` has no sleeve equity; (c) the P227 fold-in only applied its held-combined fallback when the sleeve OBJECT existed, and its closing comment certified the no-object case as safe ("the peak has not seen sleeve equity") — true when written, **falsified the day P253 made the anchors persistent**. Every restart would have re-fired this until fixed. Note the reverse hazard the fix also closes: re-anchoring on the partial equity would produce a phantom +$3,776 GAIN masking real losses all day.
- **Fix:** pure `combined_p0_equity(kraken, sleeve, held)` — fold when known; feed the HELD combined when unknown (unreadable OR not-built-yet); Kraken-only ONLY on a genuinely first-ever boot (where no combined anchor can exist). `_p0_last_combined_equity` is now persisted in the `_save_paper_positions` payload and restored in the governor section via pure `restore_p0_combined_equity()` — the P253 anchors and the value that makes them safe now survive the same restart together. The P253 daily anchor sets from the RESOLVED equity (pinned).
- **Kill switch RESET as part of this incident** (recorded manual reset, confirmation semantics `RESET-20260811`): the activation was arithmetic fiction; leaving it tripped blocks the standing keep-trading decision and trains alert-blindness (P202). Reset by state-file surgery on the volume (`kill_switch_active` false, `risk_state` REDUCED — the same conservative re-entry state `reset_kill_switch()` uses) with the engine stopped.
- **[P261b — the first fix RE-FIRED the kill 21 seconds after the reset, and the reason is the entry's own reasoning:** "no held value = first-ever boot = no anchors exist" is false exactly ONCE — the first boot after deploying this code onto a state file that already carries the combined anchors but predates the new key. Observed live 00:29:20, same −$3,776.44. Fix: `restore_p0_combined_equity` seeds the held value from the persisted **daily anchor** when the explicit key is absent — it is combined-denominated by construction and is the exact number the daily-loss comparison uses, so the first tick's daily P&L reads 0. **Operational close-out (executed 00:38–00:42 UTC by the sibling session, timing correction to this entry's pre-claimed verification):** engine stopped → second surgery (kill False, state REDUCED, verified before/after) → deploy of `eb643a7` (CI green first) → live verification: `[P261] Restored last combined equity $10,865.13`, all three first ticks fed the HELD combined ($10,865.13, not Kraken-only $7,088.69), **zero kill activations**, P0_SAFETY PASS on every chain. **A migration case is a first-boot case with pre-existing state — every "this cannot happen on first boot" argument must be re-checked against deploying onto yesterday's files.**]**
- Tests: `tests/test_p0_cold_boot_equity_p261.py` (9) — the incident's exact numbers as the truth table, first-boot semantics, both persistence halves with the restore assignment flowing THROUGH the pure function. **The first falsification probe (`False and` on the inline restore) passed the textual pins — third catch of that shape in two days (P234, P251, here); the P251 assignment-through-pure-function rule is now applied on sight.**
- **Mitigation pattern:** a comment that certifies a code path as safe ("no spurious drawdown is possible") is a CLAIM whose premises can be silently invalidated by a later change elsewhere — here, persistence added to the anchors it reasoned about. When making state durable, grep for every comment that assumed it was ephemeral.

Only unread data can. The validation read was the last unread historical window for this candidate; had it passed, the forward ledger remained the only exam left. **A candidate that passes every robustness check you can construct from its own training history has passed nothing about the future** — and the cheap, correct order is: spend the last unread historical window BEFORE wiring a forward ledger, not after (P259 wired first and read second; the right order is the reverse — one day's ledger noise, but the principle stands).

### P253. [FIXED 2026-08-09] The full-codebase read-through: a tick crash liquidated the sleeve, a refused flatten cancelled its own protective stop, and four risk controls could never fire — the whole batch fixed in one pass
Operator ordered a read-through (6 parallel subsystem audits, every actionable claim re-verified at the call site per P228) and then "address all issues found". Fixes, pinned by `tests/test_p253_readthrough_fixes.py` (42):
- **1. A tick crash — or a KRAKEN disconnect — flattened the Coinbase book.** Both early returns in `process_4h_tick` (disconnect ~main.py:5632, crash ~:5710) returned a BARE `TradeIntentV36()` (veto_active=False, target_exposure=0), which `sleeve_direction_from_intent` reads as `zero_target_exposure` → target 0 → `manage_to_signal(a, 0.0)` liquidates every routed asset. The disconnect gate tests the **Kraken** execution manager — a Kraken API outage flattening the Coinbase sleeve is the exact P195/P141 class. Rule 5 of the translator's own docstring ("missing intent must mean HOLD, not 0"), arriving through a door the docstring didn't cover: the prefetch-failure path was safe (`continue`, no intent), the crash path was not. Fix: both returns now carry `TICK_CRASH_HOLD` / `EXCHANGE_DISCONNECTED_HOLD` veto reasons, added to `_SLEEVE_HOLD_VETOES` — the sleeve holds, the venue stop keeps protecting, PATCH-8 still halts on 3 consecutive crashes.
- **2. The inverse-P207: a BLOCKED/FAILED flatten cancelled the live position's stop.** The P197 stop reconcile passed `intended_target=target_for_signal(_m_dir)` UNCONDITIONALLY — including when `manage_to_signal` returned BLOCKED/FAILED/ERROR/SKIPPED_STALE — and `ensure_protective_stop(intended_target=0)` forces `cur=0` → cancels every resting stop. So a flatten the venue REFUSED left the surviving position with no venue-resting protection for 4 hours. New pure `stop_reconcile_intended_target(status, intended)`: intent governs only on OK/NOOP (the statuses where it was acted on); anything else falls back to the snapshot.
- **3. `execute_target` could place a priceless order and act on a stale snapshot.** A failed `get_product` → `mid=0.0` → a SELL limit at ~0 is "sell at any price" (`_notional_usd` guarded exactly this; the ORDER path didn't) — now refuses `no_price`. And unlike `manage_to_signal`, `execute_target` ignored `_reconcile_ok` (its direct callers: FORCE_FLAT, the fast-risk watchdog) — sizing `delta` off a failed reconcile can overshoot into an OPPOSITE position on a venue with no reduce_only; now `SKIPPED_STALE` (P141).
- **4. `reconcile_positions` sign logic was fail-dangerous.** `contracts if side == "LONG" else -contracts` turned ANY unexpected side string (SDK enum rename, missing key) into a phantom SHORT, and a signed `net_size` double-negated (SHORT + net_size=−2 read as +2). Now: magnitude = abs(), sign by "LONG"/"SHORT" containment, unrecognized side → raise → `_reconcile_ok=False` (refusal is recoverable; a fabricated position is not). Same class as the `entry_vwap` bug documented five lines below it.
- **5. Four controls that could never fire, made real:** (a) **the 10% daily-loss kill switch** read `market_data.get("realized_pnl_today", 0.0)` — a key with NO writer anywhere (P170 shape) — now produced as UTC-day mark-to-market delta vs a persisted day-start anchor; (b) **the P0 stale-data guard** was stamped UNCONDITIONALLY every tick by `pre_tick_update` (a check that cannot fail) — now stamped only when `data_valid` and not synthetic; (c) **FastRiskTick's sleeve branch** was gated on the CACHED contract count (no `_reconcile_ok` check) so a stale-zero cache routed EXIT_ONLY into the inert Kraken body — now gated on "sleeve exists", and a watchdog flatten arms the P232 re-entry cooldown; (d) **the P237 tripwire** counted INSUFFICIENT/DEGENERATE horizons (no `vs_threshold` key → `""` → "not TRADEABLE") as GATE-CLOSED — "not enough data" could have deactivated a live asset on an outage; no-data days are now excluded and reported.
- **6. RAM-only state that disarmed on every deploy:** SOTARiskController (peak/HALTED/**the 35% kill switch** — P150 class, restart cleared an active halt) now has one-directional `to_dict/from_dict` (can re-arm/raise, never clear/lower) persisted in the `_save_paper_positions` payload; the existence fuse's `to_dict` kept only **50 records ≈ 8 days of the "28d" window** — now 400; run_live's ONLY save call sat under Coinbase connectivity (adapter down = fuse/governor state never written — P209 re-armed on a different condition) — a loop-level save now runs every tick; the daily-PnL anchor persists (same-UTC-day restore only).
- **7. Routing failure direction reversed.** `_coinbase_routed`'s "fail-closed to Kraken" comment predates Phase B: with the flag ON, an unreadable/corrupt `coinbase_routing_state.json` returning False **resumed Kraken spot entries** for assets whose positions live on the sleeve. Now: flag ON + routing unreadable → routed=True (Kraken entries BLOCKED, sleeve holds — freeze beats reopening the wrong venue), one-shot CRITICAL naming the fix; flag OFF unchanged. Also: handle leak fixed, `HMATS_DATA_DIR` honoured, and the dead `_coinbase_get_sleeve()` (would have built a SECOND unconfigured sleeve — no stop, no caps) deleted.
- **8. Offline/evidence tooling:** `rebuild_pipeline.py`'s funding merge got the causal `shift(1)` (the P247 debt "for the next parquet rebuild", now closed at source — **parquets must still be rebuilt before any future DRL/supervised run**; the current parquets carry the leaked column); the whole-column `nanmedian` NaN-fill before the causal wavelet → `ffill`; `export_regime_book_models.py` now REFUSES without `--force-retired` (re-running it would have silently resurrected the P250-retired SOL bear leg); `compute_shadow_ic`'s t-stat is now overlap-corrected (`n_eff = n/h`, the P231 arithmetic its two sibling tools already had — **pre-P253 shadow-IC t-stats are ~√h overstated**; the P199 `ml_factor` PROMOTE should be re-read under the corrected gate).
- **9. Hygiene:** the fetch-failure "reset on success" sat AFTER a `return` (unreachable — the CCXT reset fired on every 10th LIFETIME failure); `_hb_equity = _hb_eq if _hb_valid else _hb_eq` (validity discarded; now carried into `equity_history.jsonl` as `equity_valid`) + EQUITY-LOG NameError scoping; `hetzner_deploy.sh` now passes `--require-all-gates` (**~~the deploy interpreter needs mypy==2.3.0~~ — CORRECTED same day by P253b below: that design blocked every deploy from the operator machine and was replaced with a CI-green check on the deployed sha**); `latency_cost_bps` attr name in the AP-4 log; flat-signal (direction==0) no longer reads as SHORT in the reversal detector (force-closed longs but not shorts); prefetch-skipped assets stamp `SKIPPED_PREFETCH` instead of showing the previous tick's execution_status; regime-book funding refresh made per-asset (scalar day latch starved ETH/SOL); `binance_taker_flow_valid` distinguishes outage-zero from real zero; `coinbase_ma_filter_enforce: false` added EXPLICITLY to the live profile (was the one sleeve flag invisible from config).
- **Recorded, deliberately NOT changed (each a P141-class activation needing its own decision):** `gambler.allowed_regimes` names regimes in NO live GMM vocabulary (enabled feature that can never fire — annotated in config); `structure` CONFIRM direction is a quant tautology (stated at the site, the P228 `regime` treatment); fusion's `funding_rate` signal is a different series than the `funding` agent the IC tools validate; `_get_effective_position_state` in LIVE reads Kraken-shaped state so `soft_stop/gambler_exit/exit_alpha/adaptive_stop` cannot fire on the sleeve and a P0 "don't open" block translates to `veto_flat` (flatten) for routed assets.
- **Mitigation patterns:** (a) an early-return that fabricates a NEUTRAL object is a write site — trace every consumer of the sentinel it returns, because "empty" is rarely neutral downstream (here it meant "liquidate"); (b) any carve-out that lets INTENT override a SNAPSHOT must state which statuses prove the intent was acted on — an intent the venue refused is not evidence about the book; (c) when the same doctrine (P166/P231) is implemented in three tools, diff their arithmetic — two had the overlap correction, the gate that decides promotions did not.

### P253b. [FIXED 2026-08-09, same day] P253's deploy-gate design blocked every deploy from the operator machine — replaced with a CI-green check on the DEPLOYED sha; and the leak-corrected parquet rebuild ran
- **The P253 `--require-all-gates` design was wrong, verified by measurement before it ever bit:** the operator venv ALREADY HAS mypy 2.3.0 and the gate still exits 1 there — the P227 environment fingerprint (+7 phantom findings at the SAME analyzer release; a P175-style scratch diff of HEAD vs working tree on this machine showed **zero real new errors and 9 fixed**). So the two possible local interpreters both failed step 0: venv (phantom findings) and bare python (no mypy → `--require-all-gates` refusal). The mypy baseline is a fingerprint of **CI's environment**, and no local Windows/PyX.Y run can be held to it.
- **The replacement closes P187's hole in the only environment where the type gate is meaningful.** `hetzner_deploy.sh` step 0 now: (0a) resolves `origin/main` (what the server actually pulls — deploying is never a statement about the local tree, and a HEAD≠origin mismatch warns), queries the GitHub API for that sha's `codebase-invariants` + `test-suite` conclusions, and **refuses to deploy unless both are `completed/success`** — missing runs, pending runs, red runs and an unreachable API all refuse (a check that cannot run is not a check that passed, P159; emergency override `HMATS_DEPLOY_SKIP_CI_CHECK=1`, loud). This also operationalizes the P233/P252 standing rule: the deploy path now READS both workflow conclusions via the API, mechanically. (0b) the env-independent stdlib scanners still run locally via new `ci_check_invariants.py --skip-mypy` — an EXPLICIT, bannered skip, mutually exclusive with `--require-all-gates`, valid only because 0a adjudicates types in the canonical environment. Verified end-to-end: `--skip-mypy` exits 0 on the operator machine, the exclusion exits 2, and the live API check returned GREEN for `5431086`.
- **The P253 parquet debt was then paid:** `rebuild_pipeline.py --smooth 2 --skip-gmm` re-ran on the operator machine, so `{BTC,ETH,SOL}_4H_full.parquet` now carry the CAUSAL `funding_rate_zscore` (previous-day close, trailing z) instead of the P247 16h look-ahead, plus the causal ffill NaN-fill. **`--skip-gmm` was deliberate:** the funding fix touches no GMM input, and a refit could flip BIC's k on numerical noise, silently breaking the P215 rule that {GMM, parquets, checkpoints} move as ONE versioned set — the official_p221b GMMs stay paired with these parquets. Pre-rebuild artifacts preserved at `training/training_data/_p253b_backup/` (operator-local, gitignored). Any future DRL/supervised run now trains on the clean column; the DEPLOYED-model verdicts (0/9, 0/18) are unaffected — they were measured on lab-side corrected X already (P250).
- **Mitigation pattern:** a gate keyed to a baseline is only meaningful in the environment that stamped the baseline — enforcing it elsewhere converts environment drift into a permanent deploy block (or, with the old skip, into silence). Put the enforcement where the baseline lives (CI), and make every local skip explicit and loud, never inferred from a missing tool.

### P251. [FIXED 2026-08-09] The hold band evaluated a phantom position on every post-flatten tick — the P207 stale-snapshot window, found on the feed P232 built and P234 fixed
- **Observed live, twice** (2026-08-09 20:02 → 2026-08-10 00:02): `[GATE-HYST] pos=+1 ... WOULD-EXIT` while the venue reconcile four seconds later showed `positions=FLAT`. Mechanism: the sleeve reconciles in the heartbeat AFTER decide, so `market_data["sleeve_position_contracts"]` on the tick following a flatten carries the PRE-flatten snapshot — the hold band judged a position that no longer existed.
- **Why it mattered beyond a noisy log line:** a phantom `+1` with alpha landing inside the hold band would CLEAR the gate veto — and the driver would then **enter from flat at below-enter alpha**, "no re-entry credit" defeated by staleness. Same window also silently skipped the cooldown's flatten-record whenever the flatten limit had not filled by the immediate post-manage check, so the cooldown sometimes never armed.
- **Fix — intent beats snapshot (the P207 rule, applied to this feed):** pure `sleeve_snapshot_is_post_flatten_stale()` + `sleeve_position_feed()` in `main.py`; the market_data assignment goes THROUGH the feed function, which returns 0 inside the ≤1-round post-flatten window (staleness resolves toward NOT loosening; a genuinely failed flatten re-arms the band honestly at the next reconcile). Cooldown now records on flatten-SENT (`target==0`, status OK) as well as on observed fill — recording at send only ever starts the cooldown earlier, and while a position persists the cooldown is moot (entries-from-flat only).
- **The falsification that failed, and what it taught:** the first wiring pin asserted the guard's if-statement exists — and a `False and` probe **passed all three tests**. The P234 lesson applied to its own fix: a pin on source text proves the code was written, not that it runs. Restructured so the ASSIGNMENT is the pure function call; bypassing it now fails behaviorally. **When a falsification probe stays green, distrust the pin, not just the probe.**
- Tests: `TestP251StaleSnapshotGuard` in `tests/test_gate_hysteresis_p232.py` (file at 38) — truth table incl. the live incident's exact values, feed-function-is-load-bearing, sent-based cooldown record pins. NOT deployed here (rides the next scheduled deploy per the standing decision — until then each post-flatten tick emits one spurious WOULD-EXIT evidence line, which readers of `[GATE-HYST]` stats should discount).
- Numbered P251 — parallel sessions consumed P242–P250 same day.

### P250. [MEASURED 2026-08-09] The full DS lifecycle ran end-to-end (feature lab → enriched EDA → full ladder per cell → assembly) — trained models won ZERO of 18 cells outright, SOL's "+64.2% strongest candidate" is confirmed dead as the leak's third tentacle, and the roster settles
Operator asked for end-to-end feature engineering + retraining across a full model zoo. Built and ran (tag p250_full; monitors → commit `372d08c` lineage):
- **Feature lab (`training/feature_lab.py`):** 72 systematically generated candidates → AUTOMATED P164 causality gate (selection pinned so the gate tests constructions) → screening (IC floor, redundancy vs base+accepted, half-split sign stability) → 17/21/14 survivors (BTC/ETH/SOL). Two faults caught by the pipeline's own stages: the determinism assert exposed selection-dependence in the gate (fixed by pinning `top`), and inf→1e308 from a zero denominator overflowed the scaler into NaN (fixed: inf→0 + winsorize — a zero denominator is "no information", not a huge value).
- **[P250-F1b] The P247 leak's THIRD tentacle, found by the feature lab's first screening output:** the parquet's `funding_rate_zscore` column sat in **X itself**, so every MODEL cell — including the deployed SOL bear export — trained on the 16h look-ahead (P247 fixed only the rule cells and carry). X's column is now replaced in place with the causal series. **Consequence measured: SOL's bear ridge CV +5.5% → +0.3% on clean X, and the clean SOL perp assembly's validation = −22.9% vs the leaked-era +64.2% — P247's "strongest candidate ever" was the leak.** The re-exported artifact was DELETED (`configs/regimebook/SOL_bear_ridge.json`); the shadow harness correctly degrades SOL to hold-bull/flat (`flat_degraded_no_model`).
- **The ladder (operator challenge answered in code):** rules → ridge → enet → LightGBM → **RF → kNN** (added) → MLP per cell, exclusions recorded at the dispatch site (transformers data-starved at cell n; RL 0/9 twice; GP O(n³) infeasible for walk-forward; GAN era-baking); TCN/GRU remains the plan's CONDITIONED rung 6. **Result: trained models won 0/18 cells outright** (two marginal noise wins ≤+0.7% CV); hold/flat/funding rules held every material cell against 8–9 trained challengers each on enriched clean features. That is now a many-family measured verdict, not a prior.
- **Clean six-book verdicts (5th ledgered validation read):** BTC perp **+33.6%** vs B&H +20.6 / trend-only +16.6, flags NONE, pre-design +46.9 — the standing unrejected candidate; BTC spot +18.1 (no flags, loses to B&H); ETH perp +1.1 vs trend-only **+35.7** (trend-only IS ETH); ETH spot −29.1 (4 flags); SOL perp **−22.9** (ERA); SOL spot −5.0 = trend-only (ERA). **Roster for the P166 forward gate: BTC perp assembly + ETH trend-only + SOL hold-bull-only — exactly what the deployed shadow harness already records.** No harness changes needed; only the SOL export deletion.
- **Mitigation pattern:** every stage of a real pipeline is also a leak detector — the screening table (leak-derived features ranking top), the determinism assert, and the overflow crash each caught a defect the previous stage missed. And when a leak is found in a FEATURE, grep every consumer of the MATRIX it lives in, not just the named readers: this one hid as column ~97 of X through two prior fixes.

### P249. [MEASURED 2026-08-09] The label lab and the residual feature pass — meta-labeling fails everywhere (honestly), the first feature-engineering pass to clear the ladder rule lands on the SOL bear ridge
Operator asked whether we actually train models / do feature engineering; the two missing standard techniques were built and measured (design era only, purged CV, trial-counted; NO validation reads taken — that spend stays an operator-visible decision).
- **`training/label_lab.py` — triple-barrier labels + meta-labeling (López de Prado): NOT EARNED, all 12 combos negative.** Vol-scaled barriers (±1.5σ, 24-bar vertical), primary = the era-stable bull-hold leg, meta-classifier (logistic + small LGBM × thr {0.45,0.55}) predicts P(the long works). Base rates 0.46–0.52 — a coin flip the 135 features cannot call, so gating just taxes the rule: BTC −2.0..−9.9pts, ETH −1.2..−6.2, SOL **−14.6..−23.6** (worst where the bull drift is strongest — sitting out costs the most). The no-forecast-edge verdict, now confirmed at the LABEL level. Recorded with trial counts (4/asset).
- **`training/residual_feature_pass.py` — loss diagnosis + engineered features judged by the ladder rule:** losses concentrate in the bull-hold legs on all 3 (where the books are most positioned); vol texture differs sharply — **ETH loses specifically in MID-vol (−35.5% of PnL), SOL loses in LOW-vol (−59.8) and wins huge in high-vol (+157.2)** — the SOL low-vol pattern is a future filter candidate. Engineered set (per-regime crosses of top-6 IC features, dd-from-20d-high, vol-of-vol, funding×trend — all causal): **SOL bear ridge CV +5.50% → +5.85% on identical purged folds — EARNED**, the first feature-engineering pass in the project to clear the ladder rule ("engineered features earn their place only by beating the base set, else they are noise with a story").
- **Deferred, recorded:** folding the earned features into the DEPLOYED SOL export requires the runtime harness to COMPUTE them live (they are derived quantities, not stashable keys) — a small `regime_book_shadow` upgrade + tests. At a +0.35pt margin this rides as a follow-up, not a rushed change to the deploy path.
- **Mitigation pattern:** a technique "we never tried" earns a verdict, not a presumption — meta-labeling is textbook-correct and still failed here because its premise (a callable success probability) is exactly the edge this data lacks; and the ladder rule turned feature engineering from storytelling into a measurement in one afternoon.

### P240. [FIXED 2026-08-09] 74 CRITICALs nobody could act on — FastRiskTick alerted on a FLAT asset, with a percentage that could not be diagnosed
- **Live evidence:** `[FastRiskTick][LIVE] SOL: REDUCE_50 - depth_drop=66-69%(3x)` fired **74 times** between 11:10 and 12:01 UTC on 2026-08-08, right after P228 enabled the sleeve watchdog. **SOL was flat throughout, zero reduces executed**, and every line forwarded to Discord.
- **Two defects, one symptom.**
  1. **Unactionable severity.** A `REDUCE_50` on a flat asset is a no-op by construction — P227's sleeve handler already returns `FLAT / "no sleeve position"` and does nothing. Escalating that to CRITICAL is the **P202** pattern: an alert whose only resolutions are theatre or ignoring it, and a standing CRITICAL is how **P192**'s broken image build hid for weeks.
  2. **Undiagnosable content.** `depth_drop=69%` cannot distinguish a genuine liquidity collapse from a degraded feed reading — exactly the question the burst left open and which nobody could settle from the log afterwards. The raw `depth=$… vs baseline=$…` now travels with it.
- **Fix:** `FastRiskTick.evaluate(..., has_position=None)` sets **ALERT SEVERITY ONLY**. The returned action is byte-identical in every case; the risk decision is untouched.
- **The load-bearing property is the DEFAULT.** Only an explicit `has_position=False` downgrades. `None` — the default, and what any caller that forgets to pass it gets — keeps full CRITICAL severity. A downgrade must never be the default, or "quieter" silently becomes "blind". Falsification-checked: flipping the default to `False` fails the test.
- **The caller never infers "flat" from a stale snapshot.** It reads the sleeve's last **reconciled** book and passes `None` on any doubt or exception, so a position we merely cannot see keeps alerting at full severity. Reads cached state rather than forcing a venue call — this runs every 30s, and the P227 handler reconciles before it acts anyway.
- **Not a fix for the underlying trigger, and must not be read as one.** The burst stopped on its own at 12:01 (17h before this shipped), most likely when a 4H tick refreshed the anchor. Whether a 66–69% SOL depth drop is real or a degraded feed is **still undiagnosed** — this change makes the next occurrence answerable instead of silencing it.
- Tests: `tests/test_fastrisk_alert_actionability_p240.py` (16). Baseline `silent.tryexcept_count` +1 for the severity-hint guard (fails to `None`, i.e. keeps alerting).
- **Mitigation pattern:** an alert's severity should track what the operator can DO about it, not how alarming the underlying number looks. And when an alert reports a ratio, ship the numerator and denominator with it — a percentage alone cannot tell a real event from a broken sensor, and that is usually the first question asked.

- **The evidence (why this exists):** a 30d live counterfactual on the attribution logs (16h horizon, overlap-corrected t; memory note `profit_research_2026-08-08`): quant earns **+24.9bps/tick when model_alpha agrees** and **−78.9bps/tick (t=−3.42) when it disagrees**; model_alpha standalone +49.9bps/tick (t=2.91), positive on all three assets, same-day IC review 16h IC +0.289 t=2.17 edge 33.6bps. - **What shipped:** pure `sleeve_ma_filter_decision(pos, raw_target, ma_dir)` in `main.py` (P206 pattern) → `(ledger_dir, action, reason)`. Ledger claim = sleeve target with ANY disagreement zeroed — written every managed tick via `MAFilterEchoStrategy`/`build_ma_filter_shadow_harness` (`defense/strategy_shadow_v5_1.py`) to `data/strategy_shadow/ma_filter_*.jsonl`, prefix registered at BOTH `compute_shadow_ic` default sites (P192). ### P234. [FIXED 2026-08-08] P232's gate hysteresis shipped dead — it read the intent's direction field one STEP before fusion assigns it, so the hold band could never hold and every shadow line said WOULD-EXIT
- **Found by a full-codebase read-through, verified at the call site before acting (the P228 rule).** The P232 hold branch read `getattr(intent, "direction", 0.0)` inside STEP 7 (alpha gate), but `intent.direction` is first assigned from `fusion_result` in STEP 8 (`integration_v36.py:~1531`) — every assignment before that point is `= 0.0`. So `agrees = (0.0 × pos) > 0` was **always False**: enforcement could never fire at ANY `alpha_gate_hold_ratio`, and the `[GATE-HYST]` shadow line logged **WOULD-EXIT on every gate fail regardless of the signal**. The exact "every gate fail flattens the sleeve, 16bps/flap" behavior the block's own comment said it fixed.
- **Every `[GATE-HYST]` line emitted before this fix is invalid as hold-band evidence** — the WOULD-HOLD/WOULD-EXIT verdict was a constant wearing a counterfactual's name (P171/P174 family). Do not count pre-P234 shadow lines toward the enforcement decision; the evidence clock starts now.
- **Why the P232 tests passed on dead code:** they asserted source substrings (`"_hy_agrees" in blk`, `"(_hy_dir * _hy_pos) > 0" in blk`) — membership pins that cannot distinguish a live branch from a dead one. The P174 lesson, reproduced in the very entry that cited it.
- **Fix:** extracted module-level `gate_hysteresis_decision(pos, ratio, signal_direction, alpha, threshold)` (`integration_v36.py:~199`, the P206 unit-testable pattern) returning `(agrees, shadow_would_hold, enforce_hold)`; the agreement input is now `_alpha_input_direction` — the pre-fusion signal the gate itself just judged. Live behavior at default config is unchanged (ratio 0 = observation-only); what changes is that the shadow verdict is now real and enforcement is now reachable.
- **Tests rewritten behaviorally** (`tests/test_gate_hysteresis_p232.py`, 27): hold/exit/flip/zero-signal/degenerate-threshold truth table on the pure function, plus a wiring pin that the block passes `_alpha_input_direction` and never reads `getattr(intent, "direction"`. Falsification-checked: re-injecting the intent-direction read fails the pin.
- **Shared-tree mechanics (P225 shape, again):** a parallel session's commit `0d33691` (which claimed the P233 number for an unrelated CI finding) swept the half-landed pure function into its own commit mid-edit; this commit completes the wiring + tests. Hence P234, not P233.
- **Mitigation pattern:** any code that reads a field of an object being built up through a staged pipeline must check WHERE in the pipeline that field is first written — a dataclass default makes "not yet assigned" and "genuinely zero" byte-identical (the missing-vs-neutral collapse, P2/P163 family, here across pipeline STAGES instead of dicts). And a test that asserts a substring exists proves the code was written, not that it runs.
